item2: A photograph from the Photographicum Corpus of Drawings, part of the Corpus Gernsheim Collection, is designated bh_gern_074196_post. The photograph was donated by Walter and Jutta Gernsheim to the Institute on April 22, 2004. It is registered as a work of art in the Institute's catalogue under the number g-art 2004.04.22.

The drawing "Two Kneeling Male Nudes as Shieldholders" is from the private collection of the Trustees of the Chatsworth Settlement and was previously in the Devonshire Collection, William (Duke, 2) and the Lely Collection, Peter. It was created by Perino del Vaga, possibly in collaboration with Pietro Buonaccorsi. The drawing depicts two kneeling male nudes as shieldholders and is part of the vault decoration of the Castel Sant'Angelo in Rome, which was created between 1543 and 1548. 

The work was executed on white paper with brown ink and pen, brown wash. It measures 119 x 292 mm and is part of the collection M. Jaffé, The Devonshire Collection..., London 1994, Cat. 379. The Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome also holds a copy.

The administrator of the object is the private collection of the Trustees of the Chatsworth Settlement. Chatsworth House private collection is the second previous owner of the object. Previously, it belonged to the private collection of William (Duke, 2), Devonshire, who was the first previous owner. The object was previously in the private collection of Peter Lely.
The picture shows a kneeling figure.

The photograph is from the Corpus Photographicum of Drawings and is part of the Gernsheim Collection. It was donated to the museum on February 18, 2010, by Walter and Jutta Gernsheim. The image is numbered g-art and is classified under that designation.

The Gernsheim Archive's drawing catalog in Rome lists a pen drawing by Jusepe de Ribera. The work, with inventory number 5239/37, originates from the sketchbook (inv. 5239) of the Galleria Regionale della Sicilia in Palermo and depicts a group of figures. The drawing measures 135 x 256 mm and is labeled 49 D 11 (4) : 31 A 23 1.
The curator of the Palermo Galleria Regionale della Sicilia, Sketchbook (Inventory Number 5239), possesses an object with the Inventory Number 5239/37.
The picture shows four people who are inside a house.

A photograph from the Corpus Photographicum of Drawings, part of the Corpus Gernsheim, bears the number  gern_020113_post. It was donated in 2006 on June 12th by the Gernsheim family, Walter and Jutta. The photograph is part of the g-art collection.

This drawing is from the collection of drawings and prints of the State Museums in Berlin and was created by Federico Barocci. It shows studies for his famous Crucifixion in the Cathedral of Perugia. The drawing is executed in black charcoal and red and black chalk on squared, light paper. It measures 415 x 275 mm.

The drawing is slightly diagonally cut in the upper left corner, and there is a brown stain on the right edge. The drawing is firmly mounted on a collector's passe-partout. It is part of Emiliani's research on Federico Barocci and was mentioned in the publication "Federico Barocci, Bologna 1985" with catalogue number 127.
The curator of the collection of drawings and prints 295-1844 KdZ is the Print Room of the Prussian Cultural Heritage Foundation - State Museums Berlin.
The image depicts a person lying down with their legs raised, stretched out and with tense thighs.

This photograph is from the Corpus Photographicum of Drawings, a collection held by the Gernsheim Museum. The photograph, numbered , was donated to the museum in 2007 by the Gernsheim family, Walter and Jutta. It belongs to the "g-art" collection group and is therefore part of an extensive collection of works of art.

A sketchbook by Pietro Novelli, dated 1565, is in the possession of the Galleria Regionale della Sicilia in the Palazzo Abatellis in Palermo. The drawing, inventory number 1565/29, depicts the Assumption of Mary. It is executed on ivory-colored paper in brown and black ink with pen and wash technique. The dimensions of the work are 260 x 210 mm. 

The drawing was reproduced in the publication "Pietro Novelli e il suo ambiente, Palermo 1990" by the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome. It can be found there on page 419, under catalog number III.66.
The sketchbook (inv. 1565) from the Palazzo Abatellis in Palermo, Sicily, is in the possession of the administrator. It was created in 1565 and bears the inventory number 1565/29.
The image depicts the Assumption of Mary into Heaven, where she is carried by angels.

The photograph shows the Corpus Photographicum of Drawings, a significant archive of drawings from the Gernsheim Collection. The photograph was taken in 2005 and made possible by a donation from the Gernsheim family, Walter and Jutta, to the art museum. The Corpus Photographicum of Drawings is part of the Gernsheim Collection, renowned for its comprehensive and high-quality documentation of artworks.

The curator of the Kunstpalast in Düsseldorf published a graphic from the Graphic Collection in 1948. The drawing is by Giovanni Battista Gaulli, also known as il Bacciccia. It depicts the front of a letter with architectural sketches. The drawing was created with ink on paper with a pen and measures 393 x 267 mm. 

The work is part of the Kunstpalast collection in Düsseldorf and was already mentioned in the publication "The Drawings of Guglielmo Cortese and Giovanni Battista Gaulli" by D. Graf from 1976.
The administrator of the Museum Kunstpalast Graphische Sammlung Düsseldorf is the company FP 1948 r.
The image depicts an architect sketching handwriting and written text in an envelope, within a design or design sketch.

A photograph from the Photographicum Corpus of Drawings, part of the Gernsheim Corpus, depicts a work of art from the field of graphic arts. The photograph was acquired by the museum as a donation from the Gernsheim family (Walter and Jutta Gernsheim) on January 10, 2006. The photograph is designated bh_gern_154740_post and is classified under the category g-art.

The drawing "Crucifixion of Christ" was made by Bernardino Lanino and is part of the collection of the Biblioteca Reale in Turin. The depiction shows the Crucifixion of Christ and is drawn in watercolor on paper. The drawing was executed with a brush and white-primed ochre colors. It measures 500 x 390 mm and is inscribed with the inventory number 73 D 64 1. The drawing was cataloged in the publication "Italian Drawings from the Biblioteca Reale di Torino" by A. Bertini from 1958.  

The Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome also has information about this drawing.
The administrator of the Turin Royal Library is the Turin Administrator.
The image depicts the crucifixion of Christ, with Mary and John standing on either side of the cross.

The photograph depicts the work "Corpus Photographicum of Drawings" from the Gernsheim Collection. The signature is bh_gern_155910_post and the classification is g-art 2030.00.00. It is a gift from the Gernsheim family, more specifically from Walter and Jutta Gernsheim, and has been released for publication.

The drawing "Landscape with Figures" is by Remigio Cantagallina and was published in 1923. The work is part of the collection of the Biblioteca Classense in Ravenna and can be found in Volume 59-3A on page 3. The drawing is attributed to Cantagallina, and the printing plate is by him. The drawing is on paper and measures 14.1 x 20.3 cm. It is located at the Kunsthistorisches Institut in Florence, Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.

The administrator of the Ravenna Biblioteca Classense, Volume 59-3A, is Ravenna.

The Ravenna Biblioteca Classense is an archive in Ravenna.
The picture shows a landscape.
The photograph is a black and white negative from the Hertziana Library in Rome. It is numbered bhpd53430 and belongs to the art 2000.05 collection. The photograph has been released.

A former custodian of the drawing was Richard Krautheimer, after which it was in the private collection of Trude Krautheimer. The drawing was made and drawn by Anton Alexander von Werner. It depicts a view of Capri, a rocky coastal landscape, and is executed in pen and watercolor. The dimensions are 25 H 13 1. It is dated "AvW 1869" in the lower right corner.  

The drawing is now in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome and was recorded there on July 13, 2020.
The property manager is unknown. The property was previously part of a private collection belonging to Richard and Trude Krautheimer in Rome.
The picture shows a rocky coast.

The photograph originates from the Photographicum Corpus of Drawings and bears the number bh_gern_151286_post. It belongs to the Gernsheim Collection and was donated to the Art Museum by Walter and Jutta Gernsheim on December 31, 2011.  

The photograph is currently restricted and unavailable.

A drawing of a man carrying two pillars was made by Luca Cambiaso. The drawing is in yellow paper, executed in pen and watercolor. It measures 410 x 282 mm and is located in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.
The Uffizi Gallery, Florence Gabinetto Disegni e Stampe, is responsible for the administration of the object.
A digital photograph from the Hamburger Kunsthalle, acquired in 2010, depicts the artwork "Irrgang" by Christoph gesperrt. The photograph is in color and has been archived by bpk.

The drawing "Profile Studies of Female Figures" is by the Italian artist Ambrogio de Predis and is attributed to the Print Room of the Hamburg Kunsthalle. The drawing, which is on paper, grounded in silverpoint and overlaid with blue-grounded white, measures 137 x 205 mm and bears the signature "Predis". The work was previously attributed to the artist Predis, Ambrogio de.

The drawing is part of the Hamburg Kunsthalle collection and was featured in the publication "Italian Drawings 1450-1800" by D. Klemm, published by the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.
The administrator of the Hamburg Kunsthalle Print Room is the Hamburg Administration.
The picture shows a standing human figure.

The photograph is from the State Museums in Berlin - Prussian Cultural Heritage. The image shows a general view of the work "Steinkopf" by Walter Steinkopf, created between 1971 and 1980. The photograph was taken from the estate of Matthias Winner, to whom the artistic legacy of Walter Steinkopf belongs. The image is restricted. It was added to the museum's collection in 2016.

Published by the administrator of the Prussian Cultural Heritage Foundation, State Museums Berlin - Kupferstichkabinett - Collection of Drawings and Prints, this work by Charles de Lafosse is a drawing executed in black ink on green paper with watercolor washes. The horse skeleton with anatomical legend measures 391 x 510 mm and bears the signature 46 C 13 14 1 (+73 1) cst. The Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome houses the work.
The administrator of the objects is the Prussian Cultural Heritage Foundation, Kupferstichkabinett - Collection of Drawings and Prints KdZ.
The picture shows a horse.

The photograph is part of the Corpus Photographicum of Drawings, a collection held by the Corpus Gernsheim. The image is numbered and was donated to the Corpus Gernsheim on July 8, 2005. The photographers are Walter and Jutta Gernsheim. Use of the photograph is permitted.

The drawing "A Fair" is by Francesco Cecco Bravo and was published in 1871. It is part of the collection of the Edinburgh National Gallery of Scotland and is numbered RSA 187 there. The drawing was made with red chalk on paper and measures 277 x 414 mm. Keith Andrews mentions the drawing in his 1968 catalogue "Catalogue of Italian Drawings". The drawing is also in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.
The administrator of the Edinburgh National Gallery of Scotland is the RSA 187.
The picture shows public celebrations in a square.
A digital photograph from the Hamburger Kunsthalle shows the artwork Irrgang by Christoph closed off. The photograph was taken on January 28, 2010, and is in color.

The drawing "Study for Giulio Romano's Tomb" by Giulio Romano, also known as Giulio Pietro de' Gianuzzi, Giulio di Giulio Pippi, Pippi, Giulio Romano, Pippius Romanus, Julius Pippi Romano, Giulio Romano, Giulio Pipi Romano, Giulio Pippi Julius Romanus Jules Romain Giulio Pippi Giulio di Pietro de' Gianuzzi Gianuzzi, Giulio Romano, Giulio Romain, Jules Giannuzzi, Giulio di Pietro de' Giulio Romano, was created around 1534/1535. The work is part of a series that shows the design for the tomb of Gerolamo Andreasi. The drawing was executed on paper with brown ink and pen, washed in sepia. It measures 267 x 200 mm and is in the possession of the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.

The drawing is part of the collection "Italian Drawings 1450-1800" by D. Klemm and was listed in the catalog under number 255.
The curator of the Hamburg Kunsthalle Print Room is the Hamburg Kunsthalle.

The image depicts the construction of a monumental tomb.

The tombstone features a depiction of the historian Gerolamo Andrea.

The photograph shows a general view of a work of art from the estate of Matthias Winner, which is in the possession of the State Museums in Berlin - Prussian Cultural Heritage. The photograph was taken by Walter Steinkopf between 1971 and 1980. The artwork is closed to the public and was added to the collection of the State Museums in Berlin - Prussian Cultural Heritage in 2016.

The work "Skeleton Bones of the Horse with Anatomical Legends" was published by the administrator of the Prussian Cultural Heritage Foundation, Kupferstichkabinett - Collection of Drawings and Prints KdZ, State Museums in Berlin. It is a drawing by Charles de Lafosse, executed in black ink on green paper and washed with watercolor. The format is 390 x 507 mm.  

The title of the work, "Cours d'hippiatrique par M. Lafosse," is located on the upper edge of the image, centered. The work is located in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.
The curator of the collection of drawings and prints KdZ is the Berlin State Museums in Berlin - Prussian Cultural Heritage, Print Room.
The picture shows a horse.

A photograph from the Corpus Photographicum of Drawings, part of the Gernsheim Collection. The photograph is numbered bh_gern_165708_post and was announced in 2003. It comes from the collection of Walter and Jutta Gernsheim and was donated to the museum. The photograph is classified as part of the "g-art" collection.

The drawing "Study for the Face of Mary" was made by Carlo Palucci. The work is a drawing in graphite on gray paper, measuring 253 x 210 mm. The drawing is in the possession of the Pinacoteca Civica in Ascoli Piceno.

The work was listed in the 1995 catalogue "Bibliotheca Hertziana Rom" under number 127.
The administrator of the Pinacoteca Civica in Ascoli Piceno is Pinacoteca Civica 433/431.
The picture shows a face.

A digital photograph from the Hamburger Kunsthalle shows Christoph's "Irrgang" closed. The picture was taken in color on February 17, 2010. It is part of the Hamburger Kunsthalle's collection and is listed under the number art 2010.02.17.

The drawing "Study for Raphael's Painting The Holy Family from the House of Canigiani" was created in 1506. Raphael Santi, better known as Raffaello or Raphael, made the study in Urbino. The sheet depicts a downward-looking child's head and is one of the drawings that demonstrate Raphael's drawing skill. The drawing was executed on paper with chalk and measures 65 x 74 mm. It is part of the collection of the Hamburg Kunsthalle, Print Room.

The drawing is listed in the literature under the signature 92 D 19 16 31 A 22 1 (+32) D. Klemm, Italian Drawings 1450-1800, Cat. 451 in the Bibliotheca Hertziana Rome.
The administrator of the Hamburg Kunsthalle Print Room is the Hamburg Administration.
The image depicts several small, putti-like figures, depicted as Cupid or Cupids.

A photograph, digitized from the archive of the Hamburger Kunsthalle, shows Christoph Irrgang's work "Locked". The work is in the color "color" and dates from 2010. The file was digitized on February 26, 2010, and bears the internal designation "bhex-hamburger-kunsthalle-bpk-art 2010.02.26".

The drawing "The Resurrection of Lazarus" was created in the year 2000 in the workshop of Andrea Meldolla and Andrea Schiavone. The work, a drawing on paper, was executed in ink and with pen and brush. The ink drawing in gray and the pen drawing in white are prepared and mounted on brown paper. The dimensions of the picture are 225 x 202 mm.  

The drawing is in the possession of the Hamburger Kunsthalle, Print Room. It was acquired by the Hamburg Estate in the year 2000. The work is part of the exhibition "Italian Drawings 1450-1800" in the catalog under number 500. The drawing can be viewed at the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.
The administrator of the Hamburg Kunsthalle Print Room is the Hamburg Administration.
The picture depicts the resurrection of Lazarus. Jesus calls Lazarus with the words "Lazarus, come out!"

The photograph is from the Corpus Photographicum of Drawings and is part of the Gernsheim Collection. It is numbered and was donated to the collection on March 2, 2004, by the Gernsheim family, Walter and Jutta. The photograph is classified as a work of art, and the left half is restricted.

The drawing "Facade Project" is from the collection of the curator Florenz Gabinetto Disegni e Stampe degli Uffizi. It was created by Francesco Borromini and is located in Rome, Palazzo Barberini. The drawing depicts a facade project and is executed in black ink and wash with a pen. It measures 463 x 700 mm and is part of the Gernsheim catalogue list Bibliotheca Hertziana Rome.
The curator of the Uffizi Gallery, Florence Gabinetto Disegni e Stampe, manages the object U 6720A.

The image depicts an architectural model or drawing of a building outdoors.

The building is the Palazzo Barberini in Rome.

A photograph from the Photographicum Corpus of Drawings, the Gernsheim Collection, bears the number  gern_034855_post. It was donated on March 2, 2004 as a Gernsheim donation, Walter and Gernsheim, Jutta. The right half of the photograph is obscured.

The photograph belongs to the "g-art" collection and was donated in 2004.

The Uffizi Gallery's curator, Florenz Gabinetto Disegni e Stampe, has published the work U 6720A. The work is by Francesco Borromini, who is both the draftsman and the artist. The drawing depicts a facade design for the Palazzo Barberini in Rome. The drawing is black ink wash in pen and measures 463 x 700 mm. It is listed in the Gernsheim catalogue of the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.
The Uffizi Gallery's curator is the Gabinetto Disegni e Stampe in Florence. The object is cataloged under number U 6720A.

The image depicts an exterior, an architectural construction or a model. 
The image shows names of cities and villages, such as Rome, as well as names of historical buildings, such as the Palazzo Barberini.

The photograph depicts the "Corpus Photographicum of Drawings", a work from the Gernsheim Collection. It dates from 2005 and was donated to the museum by the Gernsheim family, Walter and Jutta. The photograph is numbered and belongs to the collection group "g-art".

The curator of the Gabinetto Nazionale delle Stampe F.C. r F.C. has published the work. The drawing is by Guglielmo Cortese and Courtois, Guillaume, with the draughtsman Borgognone, Guglielmo. The drawing depicts the front side of a preliminary study for the painting "The Adoration of the Shepherds" from the years 1665/1670, which is located in the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica in Rome. It is a preparatory drawing for the painting, executed in red chalk on paper, measuring 190 x 132 mm. The work is part of the Prosperi Valenti Rodinò collection and was published in the work "Disegni di Guglielmo Cortese..." by S. Prosperi Valenti Rodinò in Rome in 1979.
The administrator of the property is Rom Gabinetto Nazionale delle Stampe F.C. r F.C. 3285 r.
The picture shows a person with a head.

The photograph shows the Corpus Photographicum of Drawings from the Gernsheim collection. It is part of the collection of the Museum of Arts and Crafts in Hamburg and was donated in 2005 by Walter and Jutta Gernsheim. 

The photograph was taken on November 3, 2005, and is designated bh_gern_086283_post.

The Judgment of Paris by Annibale Carracci has been in the possession of the Fogg Art Museum in Cambridge, Massachusetts, since 1932. The drawing was acquired in 1932 from the private Loeser collection. The chalk drawing on laid, squared paper depicts Paris choosing between three goddesses. 

The drawing is tinted in red, brown, blue, pink, and yellow on a pale brown paper. It has numerous restored missing areas and several fold creases. It measures 395 x 460 mm and was executed in black chalk.

The custodian of the object is the Cambridge (Massachusetts) Fogg Art Museum. The museum has managed the object since 1932. Prior to that, it was in a private collection in Florence belonging to Charles Loeser.
The image depicts the condemnation of Paris, with Mercury also present.
On February 2, 2007, a photograph of the National Museum in Stockholm was taken. The photograph is in black and white and has been released for use.

The curator of the Stockholm National Museum NM H 82 (verso) published it in 1863. The drawing was previously attributed to an Italian private collector who belonged to Giorgio Vasari's collection. There were even earlier attributions to the Florentine draftsman Antonio di Jacopo d'Antonio Pollaiuolo. The dating of the drawing is between 1486 and 1500. On the reverse side is a garment study, a fragment of the art of drawing. The drawing is executed on blue paper in silverpoint and is part of the collection of the National Museum in Stockholm.

The artist is anonymous. The drawing was cataloged in 2001 in the publication "Italian drawings from the collection of Giorgio Vasari..." by P. Bjurström.
The curator of the Stockholm National Museum, NM H 82 (reverse), is Giorgio Vasari. The object dates from 1863 and was previously in a private collection in Italy.

The photograph is from the Corpus Photographicum of Drawings, a collection of photographs of drawings held by the Corpus Gernsheim. The image is identified as bh_gern_180482_post and belongs to the category g-art. It was donated to the Corpus Gernsheim in 2005 by Walter and Jutta Gernsheim.

The drawing "Studies for a Water-Operated Machine (?)" is by Alessandro Bibiena and was acquired by the State Graphic Collection Munich, Bibiena Production. The drawing was made by Alessandro Galli Galli da Bibiena, Alessandro Alessandro Bibiena, and Alessandro Bibiena. The work is a drawing in pencil and pen, measuring 307 x 197 mm and signed "47 D 4".

The inscription on the drawing provides information about "Explanations for the Machine". The drawing is in the possession of the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome and is part of the Gernsheim Catalogue.
The administrator of the State Graphic Collection in Munich is the Verwalter München.
The picture shows a machine powered by water.

The photograph is from the Photographicum Corpus of Drawings and belongs to the Gernsheim collection. It can be found under the number bh_gern_028241_post. The photograph was donated to the Institute on July 23, 2003, by Walter and Jutta Gernsheim. The photograph is currently restricted.

The drawing "Youth Before a Man with a Hat" is attributed to Domenico Gargiulo and is exhibited at the Florence, Gabinetto Disegni e Stampe degli Uffizi, under the inventory number 2197 F. The previous attribution to Salvator Rosa originates from the Gernsheim catalogue. The drawing was executed in the technique of brown ink, brown wash in pen on paper. It measures 76 x 74 mm and is in the possession of the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.
The curator of the Uffizi Gallery, Florence Gabinetto Disegni e Stampe, is responsible for the administration of object number 2197 F.
The picture shows an adult man interacting with a young man, a teenager.

The photograph is part of the Corpus Photographicum of Drawings from the Gernsheim Archive. It is numbered bh_gern_117789_post and was donated on January 19, 2005, by Walter and Jutta Gernsheim. The photograph belongs to the "g-art" collection and is therefore a work of art.

The drawing "Study for Gatti, Bernardino" was published by the curator of the Galleria e Museo Estense in Modena. It is by Bernardo Gatti and dates from 1560/1570. The work depicts Moses, Adam and Eve, as well as other figures, which served as a preparation for the dome painting "Assumption of Mary" in the church of Santa Maria della Steccata in Parma. The drawing is a preparatory study in the form of a drawing and consists of several fragments that were glued onto a common carrier. It is executed on paper in chalk, ink, white lead, and watercolor, which was washed and squared with pen and brush.

The drawing measures 180 x 139 mm and is in the possession of the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome. The publication can be found in the collection "Disegni della Galleria Estense di Modena" edited by J. Bentini, published in 1989.
The administrator of the Modena Galleria e Museo Estense is the Modena Galleria e Museo Estense 1039.
The image depicts representations of Moses, Adam, and Eve from the Old Testament, which are not presented in a biblical context but rather freely interpreted.

The photograph depicts a work from the Corpus Photographicum of Drawings, part of the Corpus Gernsheim. It was designated with the number bh_gern_060765_post and is part of the collection donated to the museum by Walter and Jutta Gernsheim in 2007. 

The photograph was taken on May 1, 2007, and bears the designation g-sc.

The design for a prospective dome painting is by an unknown artist and was published by the Kunsthalle Bremen. The drawing dates from between 1701 and 1800 and is Dutch. It was executed in black and white lead pencil and pen with ruled squares. The dimensions are 264 x 289 mm. The work is part of collection 41 A 44 in the Gernsheim catalogue, on page 1298, and is located in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.

The administrator of the Kunsthalle Bremen is the Bremen Kunsthalle.
The object number of the object is 63/175.
The image shows a ceiling area decorated with ornaments.

The photograph is from the Photographicum Corpus of Drawings and belongs to the Gernsheim Collection. It was registered under the number bh_gern_180483_post. The photograph is part of the "g-art" collection and was acquired in 2005 through a donation from the Gernsheim family, Walter and Jutta.

The drawing "Study for Two Boats on a River, Driving a Wheel with Water" is by Alessandro Bibiena and was produced in Munich at the State Graphic Collection. The work is part of the Galli Collection and was created by Alessandro Bibiena, the artist himself. The drawing depicts two boats on a river, driving a wheel with water. The technique is pencil and pen. The dimensions are 212 x 347 mm.
The administrator of the State Graphic Collection Munich is the city of Munich.
The picture shows ships in a sea, driven by a strong wind. Some of the ships have sails set at different angles, indicating they are sailing in different directions.

A photograph of unknown origin depicts a rare species from 1912 to 1915. The photograph was produced as a photoprint and released using the photomechanical process. The entire photograph has been fully adhered. On the reverse side is a stamp with the marking "Rs."

The draftsman Rosso, Giovanni Battista di Jacopo di Guasparre, also known as Rosso Fiorentino, il Maître Roux, Rosso, Giovanni Battista di Jacopo Giovanni Battista di Jacopo Giovanni Battista di Iacopo Fiorentino, Rosso Rosso Forrentino Giovanbattista di Jacopo di Gasparre il Rosso Rosso Fiorentino, executed the drawing "Corpse of Christ". The work was attributed to the Grahl Collection in Dresden, a private collection. The exact place of publication is unknown. The drawing dates from the 16th century and is executed in ink on paper. It is currently located in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.
The administrator is unknown. The property was previously in the private collection of August Grahl in Dresden.
The image depicts the mourning for the deceased Christ. Mary and John stand aside and look at the body of Jesus, which lies on a cloth.

The photograph depicts a work from the Corpus Photographicum of Drawings, part of the Gernsheim Collection. The image was taken on February 7, 2005, as part of the Donazione Gernsheim, Walter and Gernsheim, Jutta. The photograph is identified as bh_gern_080266_post and has been assigned to the category "g-art".

The drawing "Study for Ismael and Hagar's Garment" is from the Graphic Collection of the Kunstpalast Düsseldorf (Inv. No. FP 7910). It was made by Guglielmo Cortese and dates from the 17th century. The drawing is in chalk on grayish-brown paper and depicts a study for the biblical scene of Ismael and Hagar's garment. The dimensions are 517 x 381 mm. The drawing belongs to the collection of the Kunstpalast Düsseldorf.

The reverse side of the drawing bears the designation "Double recording, T,001". The drawing was mentioned by the art historian D. Graf in his work "The Drawings of Guglielmo Cortese and Giovanni Battista Gaulli" from 1976 and illustrated in the catalog under No. 125.
The administrator of the Museum Kunstpalast Graphische Sammlung Düsseldorf is FP 7910.

The photograph comes from the Corpus Photographicum of Drawings, a collection held by the Corpus Gernsheim. The image bears the internal number  and was donated on August 25, 2010 by the Donazione Gernsheim, Walter and Gernsheim, Jutta. The photograph is classified under the designation g-art and may be used freely.

The curator of the State Art Gallery Karlsruhe, the Print Room, published the drawing "Malvine Schrödter on the Balcony in Karlsruhe" by Anton Alexander von Werner in 1966. The drawing, made by Anton Alexander von Werner, depicts Malvine Schrödter on the balcony in Karlsruhe. The work is a pencil drawing and was marked "pc". Its dimensions are 214 x 309 mm. The drawing is part of the Gernsheim Catalogue and bears the number 61 BB 2 (SCHRÖDTER, Malvine). The Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome possesses a copy of the Gernsheim Catalogue.
The curator of the State Art Gallery Karlsruhe, the Print Room, was active from 1966 to 1915.
The picture shows Malvine Schrötter.

A rare black and white photogravure from 2018, from the estate of Hans Werner Schmidt, and released by him. It was produced using a photomechanical process and is in very good condition. The Alinari stamp (Idea F.lli Alinari Soc. An. Firenze via Nazionale 8 casa fondata nel 1854 Disegnid ei grandi maestri N. 582 Poccetti Bernardino, Firenze Galleria Uffizi Soffitto) can be seen on the photograph. The photo depicts Bernardino Poccetti's ceiling fresco in the Galleria Uffizi in Florence.

The draftsman Bernardino Poccetti created the study for a wall decoration. The drawing, designated 908 E, is in the possession of the Florence Gabinetto Disegni e Stampe degli Uffizi. The authorship of the drawing is disputed, as various sources name Bernardino delle Facciate, Bernardino delle Grotten, Bernardino delle Muse, and Bernardino Poccetti as the creator. The dating of the study is unknown.

The architectural drawing comes from the collection of the Bibliotheca Hertziana Rom and bears the signature 41A44.
The administrator is Florenz Gabinetto Disegni e Stampe degli Uffizi 908 E.
The picture shows a decorated blanket with various elements.

The plan archive of the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome was designed by Giuseppe Papillo. The architect Giuseppe Papillo participated in the architectural competition for the renovation of the Bibliotheca Hertziana in April 1995. The drawings presented here are from Papillo's design and show various views of the building, including floor plans, sections, and elevations. They illuminate the different floors of the building, from the 2nd basement to the 5th floor and the terrace.

The drawings provide insights into various areas of the building, such as the courtyard, the mask portal, and the transition to the Palazzo Stroganoff. In addition to the architectural drawings, system plans and facade elevations are also shown.

Giuseppe Papillo, the architect of the Palazzo Zuccari, planned a renovation of the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome in April 1995. His designs for the renovation were submitted as part of an architectural competition. The drawings documenting the renovation plans show various perspectives of the building, including floor plans, sections, and elevations. The sketch sheets and drawings encompass the planning of the basement, ground floor, and upper floors, as well as detailed representations of the courtyard and the mask portal.

Furthermore, the drawings document the integration of the building into the Palazzo Stroganoff and the transition to it. The plans also include system plans and facade drawings that illustrate the technical details of the renovation. The drawings of the reading room complete the documentation of the renovation project.

Published in the Getty Research Institute Special Collections in Los Angeles, the drawings originate from the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome. The collection comprises a variety of designs and studies for architectural projects created between 1765 and 1810. The works include preparatory drawings for ornaments, an altar, decorations, inscriptions, and studies for halls and portal piers. The drawings are executed in pen and watercolor.  

Among other things, there are studies for an altar, decorative designs, and preparatory drawings for a hall. Further designs show sections through churches and studies for portal piers, both right and left.

The Getty Research Institute in Los Angeles houses a collection of designs by the architect from the period 1765 to 1810. The drawings, located in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome, include preparatory sketches for various architectural projects. These include designs for ornaments, an altar, decorations, inscriptions, a hall, and cross-sections of churches. Some drawings also show studies for portal pillars.

The drawings were made with pen and watercolor on paper and are mostly used on both sides. Most sheets can be found in the Bibliotheca Hertziana with the catalog numbers T001 to T009.

The drawing "Project for a Bridge over the Vallato Ditch" by Girolamo Rainaldi dates from 1612. The watercolor wash drawing was made by Rainaldi himself and is now in the Federiciana B/3/8 of the Biblioteca Comunale Federiciana. The work is listed in the Gernsheim catalogue and was recorded by the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.
The library manager is Fano Biblioteca Comunale Federiciana. The library is located in building B/3/8.
The picture shows a map from an atlas.

A photograph from the Photographicum Corpus of Drawings, part of the Gernsheim Corpus, is identified by the number bh_gern_064752_post. The photograph was added to the collection on December 9, 2003, through a donation by Walter and Jutta Gernsheim. The photograph collection is maintained under the name "g-art".

The curator of the Staatsgalerie Stuttgart, Graphic Collection, has published the sheet. The dating is disputed and is estimated at 1601/1700. It could be a partial copy after Francesco Albani (1578). The sheet depicts a group of figures with vessels, possibly a detail of a Maniera. The drawing was executed in red chalk on paper and measures 135 x 175 mm. The provenance includes several collections, including 31 AA 23 3 (+72), 31 A 23 31 (+71), 31 AA 23 12 (+71), 31 D 11 2 41 A 77 3 71 E 12 54 1. The drawing was mentioned by Ch. Thiem in "Italian Drawings 1500-1800" (Stuttgart 1977) in catalogue no. 485. The Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome also holds the sheet.
The administrator of the State Gallery Graphic Collection in Stuttgart is the Stuttgart Administrator.
The image depicts a young woman kneeling in the typical "Serpentinata" pose, kneeling on both knees and holding a ceramic container.
A scan of the document "Sopr BAS Fi.tif" was created. The file is named "bhex-sopr-bas-fi" and was scanned in color on March 6, 2007. Access to the scan is restricted.

The draftsman Annibale Carracci created the pen drawing "Boy Pulling Off His Shirt" around 1583/1585 for the collection of the curator Florence Gabinetto Disegni e Stampe degli Uffizi. The work, dated 1583/1585, depicts a boy pulling off his shirt and was executed in red chalk on paper. The drawing measures 31.4 x 26.5 cm and is located in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.
The curator of the Florenz Gabinetto Disegni e Stampe degli Uffizi is the Florenz Gabinetto.
The picture shows a young boy wearing a shirt.

A digital photograph titled "bhex-2017-53-005" is held in the Narodna Galerija. The photograph was ordered on December 12, 2024, and is part of the collection "art 2024.12.12". The order was placed as part of project 42/2011 and the photograph was received as a gift. The full view of the photograph is restricted.

The drawing "Capitol, View from the Conservators' Palace" is by Franz Caucig and was created between 1781 and 1787. The work is a brown pen drawing on paper, executed in graphite and ink. The dimensions are 328 x 225 mm. On the back is a handwritten stamp with the inscription "K.AKAD." The artwork has been mentioned in literature, including the publication "Franz Caucig: Italian Views" by J. Röll and K. Rozman (2018).  

The drawing is part of the collection of the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome and bears the signature 61F(PALAZZO DEI CONSERVATORI) 61E(ROMA) 61D(CAMPIDOGLIO) 48C24(+726) 41A541 41A11. Further components of the signature are 61F(PALAZZO DEI CONSERVATORI), 61E(ROMA), 61D(CAMPIDOGLIO), 48C24(+726), 41A541 and 41A11.
The administration of the Ljubljana Narodna Galerija G 23 is the responsibility of the Ljubljana Administrator.

A photograph from the Photographicum Corpus of Drawings, from the Gernsheim Collection, bears the number 6530. It is a gift from the Gernsheim family, specifically Walter and Jutta Gernsheim. The photograph was taken on October 14, 2003, and shows a detail of the upper half of the leaf, which is closed.

The drawing "Standing Nude Man" is from the Uffizi Collection in Florence. It is attributed to Battista Naldini, although it was formerly attributed to Pontormo. The drawing is in chalk on paper and measures 401 x 250 mm. It is part of the "Gabinetto Disegni e Stampe" collection and has the inventory number 6603 F. 

J. Cox-Rearick catalogued the drawing in his 1981 work "The Drawings of Pontormo". The Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome also has a documentation of the drawing.
The curator is Florenz Gabinetto Disegni e Stampe degli Uffizi. The object number is 6603 F v.

The photograph is from the Corpus Photographicum of Drawings collection and belongs to the Corpus Gernsheim collection. It was registered with the number bh_gern_163630_post and dated 2005. The donors of the photograph are Walter and Jutta Gernsheim. The photograph is classified as a work of art and has the inventory number g-art 2005.11.

The drawing "Head of a Bearded Old Man" was created by Domenichino. The work is a chalk drawing on gray paper and belongs to the collection of the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome. Domenichino, who is also known as Zampieri, Domenico Giampieri, and Domenico, is a renowned draftsman. The drawing was published in 1983 as part of the Verwalter Venedig Galleria dell'Accademia 592 v. 

The dimensions of the drawing are 384 x 233 mm and it is part of the series 31 B 6 (+81 3) : 31 A 53 4 : 31 A 22 1.
The property manager for Venice Galleria dell'Accademia 592 v is the Venice Galleria dell'Accademia.
The picture shows a person whose facial expression is a mixture of joy and amazement.

The photograph is from the Corpus Photographicum of Drawings, a collection in the Gernsheim Collection. It is signed bh_gern_155351_post and was donated to the collection on July 20, 2006, by the Gernsheim family (Walter and Jutta Gernsheim). The photograph is currently restricted.

The drawing "The Sacrifice of Isaac" by Felice Giani is in the possession of the Uffizi Gallery in Florence. The drawing, executed on paper with black pen, ink, and black ink, measures 311 x 224 mm. It is part of the "Giani, Felice" collection and was created by Giani himself. The work was documented in the Gernsheim catalogue of the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.
The curator is Florenz Gabinetto Disegni e Stampe degli Uffizi with object number 9899 S.
The picture depicts the moment when Abraham raises his hand to kill his son Isaac, but God or God's hand stops Abraham's hand.

A photograph of Braun, Adolphe, from 1912/1915, made as a charcoal print, is shown here. The photograph is titled "760 raro-art" and is completely mounted. It is in very good condition.

The drawing "Head of a Bearded Man" is attributed to Giorgio da Castelfranco, also known as Giorgione. The work comes from the collection of the Florence Gabinetto Disegni e Stampe degli Uffizi. The drawing is a 31 A 22 1 and is located in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome. It is part of the collection 31 A 53 4.
The Uffizi Gallery's curator is the Gabinetto Disegni e Stampe in Florence.

The draftsman Paolo Veronese, born Paolo Caliari in 1528, created the drawing "Christus in Emmaus". The work is a drawing by the artist and was created on paper. Veronese used chalk, ink and pen to create the drawing in brown and white. The drawing is mounted and measures 249 x 290 mm. 

"Christus in Emmaus" belongs to the collection of the Hamburger Kunsthalle, Print Room. The drawing was previously presented in the publication "Italian Drawings 1450-1800" by D. Klemm from 2009 in Cologne et al.
The administrator of the Hamburg Kunsthalle Print Room is the Hamburg Administration.
The image depicts the scene of the Last Supper at Emmaus. As Christ blesses and breaks the bread, he is recognized by his disciples.

The image is identified as bh_gern_067578_post and is part of the "g-art" collection. The rights to the photograph have been released.

The drawing "Design for a Dungeon" was created in Rome in 1793 by Johann Jakob Friedrich Weinbrenner. The work was executed on pale beige paper and is sepia-toned, using brush and pen in a wash technique of both watercolor and ink. The design was published by Friedrich Weinbrenner. The drawing measures 395 x 583 mm and is part of the Kupferstichkabinett of the Staatliche Kunsthalle Karlsruhe. The work has been exhibited, including in Karlsruhe in 1966 and 1978.

The drawing is in the possession of the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.
The curator of the State Art Gallery in Karlsruhe is the Print Room. The object number is VIII 2811-3.

The photograph is from the Corpus Photographicum of Drawings, a collection that is part of the Corpus Gernsheim. It was registered on April 5, 2008, under the number  and is part of the museum's collection, which was expanded by the donation of Walter and Jutta Gernsheim to the museum.

The photograph is classified as "g-art" and was therefore classified as a work of art.

The painting "Portrait of a Woman, Half-Length" is by the artist Daniel Zeichner and was created by him in 179x. The work is a drawing in pencil and watercolor on white paper. It is part of the collection of the Leipzig Museum of Fine Arts and is registered in the museum's catalog under the number NI 8814. The painting measures 179 x 142 mm and is located in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.
The curator of the Leipzig Museum of Fine Arts is NI 8814.
The image depicts a nude human figure, representing 'Corpo humano' according to Ripa.

A photograph from the Photographicum Corpus of Drawings, part of the Gernsheim Collection, bears the number bh_gern_064769_post. It was donated on December 11, 2003, by the Gernsheim Donation, Walter and Gernsheim, Jutta. The photographs are assigned to the category g-art.

The Staatsgalerie Stuttgart, Graphische Sammlung, holds sheet C 65/1388. It is a design for the plastic decoration of an interior space. The fragment was originally kept in the private collection of Ernst Ziegler. The drawing was made by Ferdinando Bibiena. The artist is also Ferdinando Bibiena. 

The work is a preparatory drawing for the architectural drawing on white paper. The brown ink was applied with a pen. The dimensions of the sheet are 161 x 65 mm. The drawing was documented in the publication "Italian Drawings 1500-1800" by Ch. Thiem, Stuttgart 1977, under Kat. 252. The Bibliotheca Hertziana Rome has further information.
The Staatsgalerie Stuttgart houses the object C 65/1388 in its Graphic Collection. Previously, the work was in the private collection of Ernst Ziegler.

The image depicts an interior with wall decorations and a reproduced sculpture piece placed on a hermen pedestal. The door and the surrounding architecture with archivolt and cornice complete the picture.

A photograph of Philpot from before 1957, taken using the Rareties Art technique. It is an albumen print released by Giovanni Brampton. The photograph is fully mounted and shows slight toning. There is no stamp on the back.

The curator of the Florenz Gabinetto Disegni e Stampe degli Uffizi, Johann Anton Eismann, published a drawing by Johann Anton Leismann. The drawing depicts a battle and is part of the collection of drawings. It measures 45 H 3 and is located in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.
The Uffizi Gallery's curator is the Gabinetto Disegni e Stampe in Florence.
The picture shows a battle.

The photograph shows a drawing from the Corpus Photographicum of Drawings, a significant collection of drawings that is part of the Corpus Gernsheim. The Corpus Gernsheim is a collection of artworks assembled by Walter and Jutta Gernsheim. The drawing was acquired as a gift from the Gernsheim family on February 22, 2011.

The Administrator of the State Palaces and Gardens of Hesse, Schloss Wilhelmshöhe, published the drawing "Seated Beggar" by Francesco Albani in the Weißenstein Wing in 1966/82. The drawing was created by Albani, Francesco (1578) in 1966/82.

The drawing is a double impression, a supplement, and depicts a seated beggar. The work is a drawing in red chalk on chalk ground, measuring 135 x 191 mm. The drawing is listed in the Gernsheim Catalogue of the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome and the Kunsthistorisches Institut in Florence.

The property manager is the state institution Kassel State Palaces and Gardens Hessen. The administration is carried out in the Weißenstein wing of Schloss Wilhelmshöhe, and the administration data refers to the years 1966 and 1982.
The picture shows a beggar.

The photograph is from the Corpus Photographicum of Drawings collection and belongs to the Corpus Gernsheim collection. The image is numbered and was acquired on October 2, 2012, as a gift from the Gernsheim family, Walter and Jutta. The photograph is classified as a work of art and has the inventory number g-art 2012.10.02.

The work was made by Giuseppe Borsato and is part of the collection of the Kunstbibliothek of the Staatliche Museen zu Berlin - Preußischer Kulturbesitz. The drawing, dated between 1801 and 1850, depicts a design for the ceiling decoration of a theater.  

The drawing technique includes watercolor, ink on paper, and it was executed with pen and brush. The dimensions of the work are 249 x 213 mm. The artwork is located in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.
The object custodian is the Prussian Cultural Heritage Foundation, State Museums in Berlin, Art Library 5064.
The image depicts a decorated ceiling painting with ornaments inspired by plant forms.

The photograph depicts a work from the Corpus Photographicum of Drawings, a collection held by the Corpus Gernsheim. The image is internally designated bh_gern_070289_post and was added to the collection on July 1, 2007. The photograph was made possible by the donation of the Gernsheim family, particularly Walter and Jutta Gernsheim.

The drawing "Landscape Study" by Max Beckmann was published by the Bremen Kunsthalle. The work, a charcoal drawing on paper, was created in 1925. It measures 120 x 195 mm. "Landscape Study" is part of the Gernsheim Catalogue of the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.
The administrator of the Kunsthalle Bremen is the Bremen Kunsthalle. The location of the Kunsthalle Bremen is Bremen, and the object number is 32/106.
The image depicts a landscape in a temperate climate.

The photograph belongs to the Photographicum Corpus of Drawings and is part of the Gernsheim Collection. It is numbered bh_gern_063321_post and was donated to the museum on October 2, 2012, by Walter and Jutta Gernsheim. 

The photograph was acquired in 2012 as part of the "g-art" collection.

Published by the State Museums of Berlin - Prussian Cultural Heritage, Art Library, the drawing 5059 was made by Giuseppe Borsato. The dating of the drawing is between 1801 and 1850. It is a design for wall and ceiling decoration, a preparatory drawing.

The drawing is executed in pen and watercolor on paper. It measures 333 x 349 mm and is located in the Kunsthistorisches Institut in Florence, Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.
The Kunstbibliothek 5059 of the Prussian Cultural Heritage Foundation, State Museums Berlin, is managed by the Berlin Administrator.
The image depicts a wall adorned with ornamentation derived from plant forms and arranged in arabesque patterns. The ceiling is also decorated with an ornamental pattern reminiscent of antiquity.

The photograph shows a drawing from the Corpus Photographicum of Drawings. It comes from the Corpus Gernsheim and bears the number  gern_063324_post. The photograph was taken on October 2, 2012 as part of the Donazione Gernsheim, Walter and Gernsheim, Jutta.

Published by the State Museums of Berlin - Prussian Cultural Heritage, Art Library under number 5057, the drawing was made by Giuseppe Borsato. The dating of the work is between 1801 and 1850. It is a design for wall and ceiling decoration, a preparatory drawing executed in watercolor, ink, and on paper. 

The work was made with pen and brush in the dimensions 275 x 193 mm. It bears the inventory numbers 41 A 41, 41 A 44, 48 A 98 and 3. The drawing is located in the Kunsthistorisches Institut in Florence, Bibliotheca Hertziana Rome.
The administrator of the objects is the Prussian Cultural Heritage Foundation - State Museums Berlin, Art Library, with object number 5057.

The curator of the Casa Buonarroti, Florence, published a miniature drawing. Its creation is attributed to Antonio Mini, the draftsman, who was mentioned orally by Alexander Perrig on July 12, 2006. Traditionally, the drawing is attributed to Michelangelo Buonarroti. It is a study of a left ear, executed in black chalk on paper. The dimensions are 70 x 70 mm. On the back is a handwritten inscription by P. Barocchi.

The drawing is documented in several publications: P. Barocchi, Michelangelo e la sua scuola, Florence 1962, Vol. 1, Cat. 229, and Ch. de Tolnay, Corpus dei disegni..., Novara 1975-80, Vol. 2, Cat. 311. It is located in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.

A photograph of Philpot, P730, dating from 1953/1956, is a rare album print. The photograph was released by Philpot, Giovanni Brampton. It is fully mounted and shows slight fading. On the back is a stamp with the K-Rs stamp.

The draftsman Leonardo da Vinci, from the circle of the artist, created the work "Female Head". The drawing is part of the collection "Gabinetto Disegni e Stampe degli Uffizi" in Florence and was illustrated by J. B. Philpot in 1870 in his work "Fotografie dei disegni originali" on page 46. The work is also in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.
The Uffizi Gallery's curator is the Gabinetto Disegni e Stampe in Florence.

The work "Historical Scene" is by Raphael, executed by his pupils. It is a drawing on chamois-colored paper, executed in pen and watercolor. The dimensions of the work are 261 x 413 mm. The artwork is in the possession of the State Palaces and Gardens of Hesse, Wilhelmshöhe Palace, in the Weißenstein Wing, Collection KI 9629 r.
The property manager is the Kassel State Castles and Gardens Hessen. The person responsible is Wilhelmshöhe Palace, more specifically the White Stone Wing. The internal reference number is KI 9629 r.
The image depicts a representation of a historical event.

The photograph depicts Philpot P263, a rare artwork from the Rare Books Department, dating back to before 1957. It is an albumen print by Philpot, Giovanni Brampton. The photograph is fully mounted and shows slight discoloration. The photographer's stamp is missing.

The curator of the Florenz Gabinetto Disegni e Stampe degli Uffizi, Giovanni, has published a drawing by Do, Juan Dò, Giovanni Giovanni Do ulan500115464. The drawing depicts the Sermon on the Mount by John the Baptist and is from the field of drawing. The drawing bears the inscription 73 C 11. J. B. Philpot photographed the original drawing in Florence in 1870, as can be seen on page 34 of his work "Fotografie dei disegni originali". The Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome possesses a copy of the drawing.
The Uffizi Gallery's curator is the Gabinetto Disegni e Stampe in Florence.
The picture depicts John the Baptist preaching, possibly with Christ among the listeners.

The design for a window grille is by the artist Fra Severo Bianchedi. The drawing was published in 20 in Ms.657 volume of the Biblioteca Classense in Ravenna. It is executed in ink and wash on paper and measures 425 x 289 mm.  

The drawing is in the Kunsthistorisches Institut in Florence, more precisely in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.
The Ravenna Biblioteca Classense, signed as vol.Ms.657, houses an object assigned to the administrator.

The image depicts a representation of the human life cycle, from childhood to old age, with a variety of figures portrayed in different poses and with varying expressions. Some figures are depicted wearing garments and head coverings, while others are shown nude or in simple clothing.

The photograph is from the Corpus Photographicum of Drawings and belongs to the Gernsheim Collection. It has the catalogue number  and was acquired on March 24, 2011 as a gift from the Gernsheim family, Walter and Jutta. The photograph is part of the "g-art" collection.

The administrator of the Wormser Stiftung Kunsthaus Heylshof published the drawing "Sea Gods" by Louis Joseph Le Lorrain. The drawing dates from 155 and was executed by Le Lorrain in black and gray chalk on paper with brushes. It measures 347 x 462 mm and is listed in the Gernsheim catalogue of the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.
The Kunsthaus Heylshof, located in Worms, is managed by the Worms Stiftung. The foundation is associated with the address 9/W 155.
The image depicts the water gods Neptune and his surroundings.

A photograph from the Photographicum Corpus of Drawings, part of the Corpus Gernsheim Collection, bears the signature bh_gern_118061_post. It comes from the Donazione Gernsheim collection, Walter and Gernsheim, Jutta and was donated on January 28, 2005. 

The photograph is part of the art category "g-art".

The reverse side of the drawing "Beinstudie" is by the artist Piazzetta. The work was created around 1200 AD in the style of drawing on paper. It is executed in blue paper, black and white, with chalk and charcoal. The drawing measures 273 x 347 mm and bears the signature 31 A 22 5. It is part of the collection of the Galleria Estense di Modena and was documented in the work "Disegni della Galleria Estense di Modena" by J. Bentini (ed.) from 1989, page 260. The Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome has another copy of the drawing.
The administrator is the Modena Galleria e Museo Estense 1200.

It has the inventory number  and was acquired in 2005 as a gift from the Gernsheim family, Walter and Jutta. The photograph belongs to the "g-art" category and is therefore classified as a work of art.

The drawing "Rolling Landscape with Abbey and Shepherds" is by Giovanni Francesco Grimaldi, a Bolognese draftsman. It was published by the Munich State Graphic Collection, under inventory number 2906. The drawing was created as part of the production of Grimaldi's works. It is a pen drawing washed with watercolor. Measuring 270 x 371 mm, it depicts a rolling landscape with an abbey and shepherds. The work is listed in the Gernsheim catalogue and is held in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.
The administrator of the State Graphic Collection Munich is the Munich Administration.
The picture shows a landscape with a tower or a castle.

The photograph is from the Corpus Photographicum of Drawings, a collection that is part of the Corpus Gernsheim. The image is numbered and was acquired on June 24, 2003 as a gift from the Gernsheim family, Walter and Jutta. The image is currently restricted.

The standing male figure in antique costume is a drawing by Andrea Commodi, made in Florence. The work was catalogued in 1994 by the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome and bears the number D 79 there. The drawing measures 348 x 230 mm and is executed on paper in pencil, pastel, and black pencil. The work was acquired for the collection of the Florence manager Gabinetto Disegni e Stampe degli Uffizi.
The curator of the Florence Gabinetto Disegni e Stampe degli Uffizi is the Florence Gabinetto.
The picture shows a standing figure.
A photograph of the Kunstpalast Museum, number 174/8076-30, from 1995, is on display. The photograph is currently restricted.

The drawing "Studies of the Legs of a Figure Turning to the Left" is a preparatory sketch by the artist Giuseppe Passeri. It is in the possession of the Graphic Collection of the Kunstpalast Düsseldorf. The back of the drawing bears the inscription "Passeri, Giuseppe Zeichner". The drawing was executed in white chalk on blue-green paper and measures 420 x 282 mm.  

Dieter Graf, who published the drawings of Giuseppe Passeri in Kunstmuseum Düsseldorf III,5, Düsseldorf 1995, lists this drawing under number 1060. The Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome also has a copy of this drawing.
The administrator of the Museum Kunstpalast Graphische Sammlung Düsseldorf is the KA (FP) verso.

The photograph is part of the Corpus Photographicum of Drawings and originates from the Gernsheim Collection. The image is numbered and was donated to the museum on June 24, 2003, by the Gernsheim family (Walter and Jutta). The photograph is currently restricted.

The drawing "Reverse of Head and Arm Studies" by Andrea Commodi dates from the 18th century. It was acquired by the curator of the Uffizi, Florence Gabinetto Disegni e Stampe, and is part of the "Commodi" collection. The drawing is executed on paper and depicts head and arm studies in ink, pencil, and pen. The dimensions are 257 x 193 mm. Further information about the drawing can be found in the publication "G. Papi, Andrea Commodi, Florence 1994, Kat. 89" by the Bibliotheca Hertziana Rome.
The Uffizi Gallery's curator is the Gabinetto Disegni e Stampe in Florence.

A photograph from the Photographicum Corpus of Drawings, part of the Corpus Gernsheim Collection, bears the number  gern_149310_post. It was donated to the museum on March 14, 2005, by Walter and Jutta Gernsheim. The photograph belongs to the "g-art" category.

The drawing "Front side of a preliminary study for the painting Mary with Child and the Saints Carlo Borromeo, Filippo Neri, Dominic and Blessed Felix" is by Guglielmo Cortese and was created in Rome in 1677. The drawing "Christ Child Sitting on a Cushion" is a copy after Perino del Vaga's painting "Holy Family" in the Musée Condé in Chantilly. The work comes from the workshop of Perino del Vaga and was executed by Pietro Buonaccorsi. The drawing was made on whitish paper with red chalk, ink, and pen and measures 166 x 100 mm. The drawing was part of the private collection of Nicolaes Anthoni Flinck and was later transferred to the collection of the Trustees of the Chatsworth Settlement. 

In the 18th century, the drawing was in the collection of William, the 2nd Duke of Devonshire, before finally entering the collection of Chatsworth House. The drawing is documented in various publications about the collections in Chatsworth House and about copies after Perino del Vaga, including the works of M. Jaffé and A. Braun.

The current custodian of the object is the private collection Chatsworth House, represented by the Trustees of the Chatsworth Settlement. Previously, the object was in the possession of the Devonshire family. William, the second Duke of Devonshire, was the second previous owner of the object. He acquired it in the period of 1723/1724. The first previous owner was Nicolaes Anthoni Flinck, who kept the object in his private collection.

The manuscript, produced by Johannes and Giovanni Grevembroch in 1760, contains a collection of drawings dealing with washbasins and fountains in Venice. The drawings, watercolored on paper, document details of water installations in various palaces, churches, and on islands. The objects depicted include washbasins in the house of Rosso Marin, in the house of the Dandolo family, on Isola della Certosa, and in the refectory of Santo Stefano. Furthermore, there are drawings of fireplace and wall basins in the Palazzo Ducale, the Palazzo Contarini, and other Venetian buildings.

The drawings are accompanied by precise descriptions and details about location and date. Some sheets are adorned with coats of arms and inscriptions that provide clues about the owners and the context of the depicted objects. The manuscript was dedicated to Pietro Gradenigo, the administrator of the Museo Correr e Quadreria Correr, and is now housed in the Biblioteca Ms. Gradenigo in Venice.
The administrator of the Venice Museo Correr e Quadreria Correr is the Biblioteca Ms. Gradenigo Dolfin 229.

A manuscript, watercolored by Giovanni Grevembroch and produced by Johannes Grevembroch in 1760, is in the possession of the Museo Correr e Quadreria Correr in Venice. It is titled "Studies of Family Magnificences Preserved Among the Modern Cloisters and Palaces of Venice" and is adorned with the coat of arms of the Gradenigo family. The manuscript contains drawings of washbasins, fireplace pieces, and fountains in various buildings in Venice, including the Doge's Palace, the Church of Santa Maria Gloriosa dei Frari, and San Michele in Isola.

The drawings are detailed and depict the artful architecture and furnishings of the Venetian buildings. Many drawings have inscriptions with information about the location, date, and artist. Some drawings are adorned with Doge's coats of arms, which highlight the importance and status of the buildings. A dedication to Pietro Gradenigo and other family members can be found on the title page.
The administrator of the Venice Museo Correr and Quadreria Correr is the Biblioteca Ms. Gradenigo Dolfin 229.

A manuscript from 1760, produced by the brothers Johannes and Giovanni Grevembroch, is located in the Biblioteca Ms. Gradenigo Dolfin at the Museo Correr in Venice. The drawings are detailed and showcase the artful craftsmanship of the marble and stonework.

The Biblioteca Nazionale Centrale di Firenze holds a collection of drawings by Bernardo Puccini, a Florentine artist active around 1576/1600. These drawings, preserved in the Palatini manuscripts, illustrate various machines and technical devices. They include designs for water mills, pumps, bridges, and lifting mechanisms. Puccini's drawings are notable for their technical detail and their use of metalpoint on parchment.

The drawings encompass a wide range of subjects, from simple tools to complex engineering projects. Some examples include designs for ship cranes, four-wheeled wagons, rope ladders, devices for moving heavy loads, and systems for raising water. Puccini's work offers valuable insights into the technological advancements and engineering practices of 16th-century Florence. His drawings have been studied by scholars such as P.L. Rambaldi and D. Lamberini, who have published analyses and interpretations of his work.
The administrator of the Florence National Central Library is the Florence National Central Library Palatino 1077.

The work presented here, a catalogue of drawings held by the Biblioteca Nazionale Centrale di Firenze, was compiled by Bernardo Puccini, the administrator of Florence, around 1576/1600. It contains detailed descriptions and drawings of mills, water pumps, bridges, and other technical devices. The drawings, executed in pen and metalpoint on parchment, shed light on the technical innovation and engineering knowledge of the time. The collection is a valuable source for the history of technology and architecture.

The drawings are recorded in various hand drawings and are numbered, referring to the pages and the respective drawing. In addition to the drawings, the annotations provide source references for the respective drawings and their authors. The collection is a valuable testament to the technical development of the 16th century and offers a glimpse into the minds of the engineers and architects of that era.

Published in the Biblioteca Nazionale Centrale Palatina in Florence, this collection of drawings, attributed to Bernardo Puccini, dates from 1576/1600. The works depict various machines, including watermills, pumps, bridges, and lifting devices.  The drawings are executed in black metalpoint on parchment using a pen and ink. They measure approximately 300 x 208 mm and are currently housed in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.

The collection includes numerous drawings of watermills, pumps, and lifting devices, illustrating Puccini's interest in mechanical engineering. The work "Disegni ingeneria civile e militare (De ingeneis, lib. III, lib. IV Opusculum de Architectura)" by Francesco di Giorgio Martini, edited by L. Bellosi, contains a collection of drawings that illustrate civil and military engineering of the 15th century.  The subjects include wells, water systems, fortifications, ship constructions, and machines for lifting weights.  The drawings, executed in parchment and ink, show the detailed planning and construction of the works.  

Martini, a Florentine artist and architect, was a significant representative of the Renaissance. His drawings are not only technical documents but also works of art that demonstrate the sophistication and engineering knowledge of his time.  Especially noteworthy are the drawings of divers, oar-powered ships, catapults, a ladder on a cart, and a machine driven by human or animal power. These drawings provide insights into the technical innovations and technological possibilities of the 15th century.
The librarian of the library is Florenz Biblioteca Nazionale Centrale Palatino 767.

The drawing "Two Studies of the Back View of a Seated Woman" is by Agostino Carracci and was acquired between 2000 and 1902 by the collection of drawings and prints of the Kupferstichkabinett of the State Museums in Berlin. Previously, it was in private collections in Berlin and Milan. The drawing on light brown paper is 269 x 354 mm in size and shows two studies of the back view of a seated woman. It shows some damage, including masked framing lines, brown spots on the right side, small losses on the left side (ink damage) and a cut off left upper corner. 

On the back of the drawing, some inscriptions and stamps can be seen. It bears the inscription " [...]acci" left bottom in brown, "Ago Cara" right bottom in red, "N 182" and further inscriptions like "Agostino (Bodmer)" and "Earlier: Passarotti?" (John Gere)". Furthermore, there are stamps from Lugt 1612 and Lugt 1223 as well as a stamp of the Bibliotheca Hertziana Rom.

The drawing "Frieze-like Wall Decoration with Festoon, Reclining Female Figures and Eagles" dates from 1902 and is in the possession of the State Museums in Berlin, Print Room - Collection of Drawings and Prints. It formerly belonged to the private collection of Adolf von Beckerath. The work has been attributed to Perino del Vaga, although earlier attributions exist to Polidoro Caldara. The pen and ink drawing on paper depicts a frieze-like wall decoration with festoon, reclining female figures and eagles. It is firmly mounted with a vertical fold line in the middle. The lower right and upper corners, as well as a missing section on the left edge, are missing. 

On the back of the mount is a stamp with the addition: "From the collection of A. v. Beckerath". The drawing is executed in brown ink, with washes, over a preliminary drawing in black pen. The dimensions are 9.2 x 25.9 cm. The drawing bears various inscriptions, including "questo friso eie fato a roma / e fraca (...) loma di eia / 1552 // allo mese di magio / alle (...)go", "Perino lower left" and "Polidoro lower right".

The administrator of the objects is the Prussian Cultural Heritage Foundation, Kupferstichkabinett - Collection of Drawings and Prints. The object was acquired in 1902 under the designation KdZ 5513. Previously, it was in a private collection in Berlin, the Beckerath Collection of Adolf von Beckerath.

The curator of the London National Gallery published a painting in 1982 that was made by Sandro Botticelli or his workshop. It is an oil painting on poplar wood measuring 59 x 40 cm. The painting is a double portrait, depicting both a portrait of a young woman and an allegorical figure. The work was dated after 1480 and was already mentioned by Lightbown in his work "Botticelli" (Volume 2, Catalogue C6/C7) and in the complete illustrated catalogue of the National Gallery by Baker and Henry (London 2002, page 63). 

The Kunsthistorisches Institut in Florence, Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome, owns two further variations of this painting. The first variation, with the catalogue number "cfi,T,001", also depicts a portrait of a young woman. The second variation, with the catalogue number "cfi,T,002", depicts a winged allegory with an armillary sphere. This variation has also been referred to as a correction of the first variation.
The administrator of the London National Gallery is the institution London National Gallery 2082.

The painting "Duchess Anna Amalia of Saxe-Weimar-Eisenach and her Traveling Companions in the Park of the Villa d'Este in Tivoli" was painted in 1789 by Johann Georg Schütz. The work is an oil watercolor on paper and depicts the Duchess with her friends in the park of the Villa d'Este in Tivoli. It is a variation of a motif that Schütz had previously painted in Düsseldorf. The painting was part of a private collection in Rome before it entered the collection of the Bibliotheca Hertziana. 

It is known that the Duchess and her company were at the "Rotonda dei Cipressi" on May 1, 1789, to hear Goethe's Tasso. This event may be the occasion for the painting. The work has been exhibited in Weimar and Rome. Gerhard Bott wrote about the painting in his publication "Duchess Anna Amalia of Saxe-Weimar and her Friends in the Park of the Villa d'Este in Tivoli".

The administrator of the object is the Bibliotheca Hertziana Kunstbesitz, Rome. The object was last part of a private collection in Rome belonging to Frida Mond since 1895/1896. 

The previous owner of the collection was Karl Glingler, also from Rome.

This painting by Johann Georg Schütz depicts Duchess Anna Amalia of Saxe-Weimar-Eisenach and her traveling companions in the park of the Villa d'Este in Tivoli in 1789. It is a variation of a motif also on view at the Goethe Museum Düsseldorf. The work was acquired by the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome and was previously found in a private collection in Rome and the Glingler Collection in Rome. The watercolor is 56.8 x 77 cm in size and bears the signature "G. Schütz fec./Romae 1789" in the upper left corner.

Schütz painted the picture in May 1789 in the "Rotonda dei Cipressi" during the Duchess's and her friends' stay in Rome to hear Goethe's Tasso. The painting has been exhibited in shows such as "Anna Amalia, Carl August and the Emergence of Classicism 1757 - 1807" at the Schlossmuseum Weimar. It is documented in the Weimar Classic Foundation Weimar and was described by Gerhard Bott in "Miscellanea Bibliothecae Hertzianae".

The custodian of the object is the Rom Bibliotheca Hertziana Kunstbesitz. Previously, the object was in a private collection in Rome, which belonged to the Mond family since 1895/1896.

Before that collection, the object was part of a private collection in Rome belonging to Karl Glingler.
