A digital photograph from the Bibliotheca Hertziana, identified as bhim00038778.tif, depicts a work of art photographed on April 24, 2019. The color photograph is from the 117/2019 photo campaign by Enrico Fontolan and shows a view of the artwork without a frame. The photograph has been released.

The curator of the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica, Palazzo Barberini, acquired the painting "Saint Agnes Refuses to Worship the Pagan Gods" in 1971. The work comes from the workshop of Andrea Camassei and is an oil painting on canvas. Measuring 178 x 233 cm, it is a significant example of 18th-century art. It was previously in the private collection of Francesco Barberini Junior in Rome.

"Saint Agnes Refuses to Worship the Pagan Gods" is documented in the catalog "Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica. Palazzo Barberini, i dipinti. Catalogo sistematico" by L. Mochi Onori and R. Vodret (eds.) from 2008, on page 118. The Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome has further information about the painting.

The curator of the Rom Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica Palazzo Barberini is Francesco, Junior from the private Barberini collection. The object was acquired in 1971 by the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica Palazzo Barberini (Barberini) in Rome.

A digital photograph from the Bibliotheca Hertziana, with the image number bhim00049086, shows the back of a work of art. The photograph was taken on April 15, 2022, under the inventory number P0006687_inv_1317v. The photograph is in color and comes from the 37/2021 photo campaign by Enrico Fontolan, which took place in September 2021. Permission has been granted for the full view of the back.

Reading Maria is an oil painting on canvas by the artist Pierre Subleyras. The painting depicts the Holy Mary reading and measures 73 cm in height and 60 cm in width. It is located in the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica in Rome, Palazzo Barberini. The work was created in 1317 by Pierre Subleyras.
The administrator of the Rom Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica is the Palazzo Barberini.

A digital photograph from the Bibliotheca Hertziana, identified as bhim00037127.tif and bhim00037127 art, was taken on October 24, 2018. The photograph, numbered HER0292a.tif, depicts a colored work by the artist Enrico Fontolan from the photo campaign 25/2018. It shows a full view of the artwork without a frame. Permission for the use of the photograph was granted on August 8, 2018.

"Saint Margaret of Cortona Discovering the Corpse of Her Husband" is an oil painting on canvas measuring 120 x 145 cm. The painting was published in 1956 by the administrator of the Rome Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica, Palazzo Barberini. Its creation is attributed to Benefial, Marco Maler, Benefialle, Marco, and Beneficiali, Marco. The work is part of the collection of the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica, Palazzo Barberini. 

Further information can be found in the work "Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica. Palazzo Barberini, i dipinti. Catalogo sistematico" by L. Mochi Onori and R. Vodret (eds.), published in 2008 in Rome, page 88. The Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome holds another source on this painting.
The administrator of the Rom Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica is the Palazzo Barberini. The address is Palazzo Barberini 2394 1956.

A digital photograph of the Bibliotheca Hertziana, designated bhim00028054.tif, is from the "chi xart" series and was taken on October 13, 2016. The photograph shows a general view and is in color. It was created and released by Enrico Fontolan in September 2016 as part of the photo campaign 46/2016.

In Rome, in the church of San Francesco di Paola, there is a chapel with a panel painting on the left wall above the entrance. The painting depicts the archangel Michael giving a hood to Francis of Paola. The panel painting is by Giacomo Triga and is oval in shape. 

The painting is titled "Francis of Paola" and is located in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.

A digital photograph of the Bibliotheca Hertziana with the signature P0021858.tif exists. The photograph was taken on July 8, 2024, by Enrico Fontolan and shows a full view with frame. The image was released on November 22, 2024. The artwork is numbered 2024.11.22.

The painting "Venetian Wedding" (Spozalizio a Venezia) by Alessandro Milesi was purchased in 1897 by the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna in Rome. The oil painting on canvas measures 140 x 207 cm. The work bears the signature "A. Milesi 1897" in the lower right corner.

The work was exhibited at the II Biennale di Venezia in 1897 in Venice. It is in the collection of the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna in Rome and has been mentioned in publications such as "Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna. Le collezioni. Il XIX secolo" (Rome 2006).
The curator of the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna in Rome is responsible for the object "Purchase 1897". This object was acquired in 1897.
A photograph by Prudence Cuming Assoc. Ltd from London dates from 2007. It was taken on January 10th. The photograph depicts art.

Luca Giordano's painting "Marcus Curtius Leaps into the Chasm" was created around 1662. The oil painting on canvas measures 180 x 237 cm and is part of the collection of the stewards of the London Merchants' Hall Walpole Gallery. The painting depicts the Roman hero Marcus Curtius leaping into a chasm to fulfill an omen sent by the gods. The depiction is documented in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome and was mentioned by Ferrari, O. and Scavizzi, G. in their work "Luca Giordano - The Complete Works, Vol. 1" from 1992 with the catalogue number A316.
The manager of the London Walpole Gallery is Walpole.

A rare photograph of Alinari Anderson, taken before 1957, is preserved in an albumen print. The photograph is numbered 2423 and is completely mounted. It shows a faded appearance and there is no stamp.

The curator of the Galleria dell'Accademia in Venice has released the painting "Sacra Conversazione with John the Baptist and Saint Jerome". The painting was made by the brothers Benedetto Diana and Benedetto Rusconi. It is a panel painting on wood, measuring 78 x 95 cm. The work was exhibited in 1955 at the Moschini Marconi exhibition, catalogue number 129. The Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome has documentation of the painting. 

The depiction shows a "Sacra Conversazione" with John the Baptist and Saint Jerome.
The manager for the Venice Galleria dell'Accademia is located in Venice. The exact address is Galleria dell'Accademia 84.

A photograph of the Bibliotheca Hertziana, taken on January 16, 2007, shows the artwork "art-e". The photograph is in color and Ektachrome format. It was created by Harry Zdera and is a reproduction. Use of the image is not permitted.

The former Jesuit church of St. Ignatius in Landshut houses a painting by Joachim von Sandrart the Elder. The work, created in 1644, depicts "The Care of Sebastian" and is an oil painting on canvas. The dimensions of the painting are 11 H x 63. It is now located in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.
A black and white photograph from 1971 shows a full view of the BAS NA Camp. The photograph is restricted.

The Church of Chiesa della Nunziatella in Naples houses a painting by Francesco de Mura. Created in 1732, it depicts Saint Francis Xavier preaching as a missionary in India. The oil painting on canvas measures 11 H (FRANCIS XAVIER) 41 2 and is located in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.
A photo from 1972 shows a detailed section of the camp layout plan for camp BAS NA 5294. The photo is in black and white, and part of the detail is obscured.

In 1760 Francesco de Mura painted the painting "Martyrdom of Saint Barbara". The oil painting on canvas measures 11 H x 68 cm. The work is in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome. The painting depicts the scene of the martyrdom of Saint Barbara in Naples, more specifically in the church of Chiesa della Nunziatella, in a transept.

A rare photograph of Alinari Anderson from the period 1940 to 1944 is in the albumen print. The image is blocked as 4323 and completely pasted over. The photograph shows clear signs of fading and yellowing. Two adhesive labels are stuck on top of each other on the back.  A stamp is visible on the back.

Saint George is a panel painting by Andrea Mantegna, described in 1955 by Moschini and Marconi in their catalogue number 148. The painting was exhibited in the Galleria dell'Accademia in Venice and is now in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome. The work is on wood and measures 66 x 32 cm.

The depiction shows Saint George.
The administration for the Venice Galleria dell'Accademia 98 is handled by the Venice manager.

A rare photograph of Alinari Anderson from between 1922 and 1933 is part of the album. It is an albumen print, which may have been a gift. The photograph is in the Kunsthistorisches Institut in Florence and comes from the estate of Dr. Gustav Ludwig. Release was granted by the estate of Dr. Gustav Ludwig. The photograph is fully mounted and shows slight discoloration and slight toning. Parts of the photograph are partially stamped with the stamp "K: Rs.".

The panel painting "Entombment of Christ" was created by the painter Matteo Galasso di Piva. The work is part of the collection of the Ferrara Pinacoteca Nazionale and was recorded by the Fondazione Zeri. The dimensions of the painting are 130 x 215 cm. It is located in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome. As an alternative, attribution to Marco Zoppo has been discussed.
The Ferrara National Picture Gallery is managed by the Ferrara Administration.

A rare photograph of Alinari Anderson from the period between 1940 and 1944. It is an albumen print, fully mounted and faded. There are two adhesive dots on the back, stuck together. 

The album stamp is present.

The painting "Visitation" by Fernando Gallegos was exhibited at the Museo del Prado in Madrid. The work is a painting and dates from the year 73 A. 67. The creation of the painting is attributed to the artist Fernando Gallegos. Information about the painting can be found in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.
The manager of the Madrid Museo del Prado is called Madrid Manager.

A digital photograph, taken with a flash, shows a detail from the painting "Pala degli Eremiti" by Hieronymus Bosch. The image is part of the collection and bears the number 2013.03.25. The photograph was taken by Alessia Polesel in 2012. Copyright for the image belongs to Rodolfo Polesel. The right wing of the painting is closed to the public.

The painting "Saint Anthony" by Hieronymus Bosch is located in the Doge's Palace in Venice. The work was created in 1505 and is part of a hermit triptych, consisting of three panels. The paintings depict Saints Anthony, Jerome, and Egidius. The triptych is a panel painting on wood and was painted with oil. The paintings are in the possession of the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome and measure 29.5 x 85 cm ("Saint Anthony"), 60 x 85 cm ("Saint Jerome"), and 86.5 x 29 cm ("Saint Egidius"). 

The artworks were mentioned by U. Franzoi in his publication "History and Legend of the Doge's Palace of Venice" from 1982.

A digital photograph, taken with flash, shows a section of the Pala di Santa Liberata by Hieronymus Bosch. The photograph is numbered bhex-polesel-2012-51-52-53-dvd1-44 and was taken on March 25, 2013, by Alessia Polesel. The image is in color and shows the right wing of the Pala, which is however closed.

The triptych of Saint Liberata is located in the Doge's Palace in Venice and was created by Hieronymus Bosch between 1500 and 1504. It is an oil painting on wood and consists of three panels. The triptych is 11 HH (WILGEFORTIS) 61 : 25 I 5 25 I 1 98 C (JULIA) 61 in size. P. Reuterswärd, Hieronymus Bosch, 1970, Cat. 30 and U. Franzoi, Storia e leggenda del Palazzo Ducale di Venezia, Verona 1982, No. 285F document the work.  Other paintings by Bosch are also on display in the Doge's Palace, including the painting "Saint Anthony" (27.5 x 105 cm) and the painting "Crucifixion of Saint Liberata" (63 x 105 cm). 

The Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome owns other works by Bosch, including the painting "The Harbor" (164 x 28 cm).

A digital photograph, archived in the Bibliotheca Hertziana under the designation bhim00027278.tif, depicts a detail of Roberto Sigismondi's face. The photograph was taken in color on July 29, 2016, and is licensed under "art". Permission for the publication of the photograph was granted in December 2015.

The donation to the Museo Regionale della Sicilia in Palermo took place in 1906. Prior to that, the painting was in a private collection. The artist of the work is Antonello da Messina, a prominent painter of the Italian Renaissance. The painting, created between 1473 and 1477 in Venice, depicts an oil painting on wood. 

Measuring 45 x 34.5 cm, the work is part of the Museo Regionale della Sicilia's collection and was documented in the catalog "Palazzo Abatellis, Palermo" by G. C. Argan et al. (1991).

The administrator of the property is the Palermo Galleria Regionale della Sicilia. The property was donated in 1906. Prior to that, it was in a private collection in Palermo, possibly belonging to Di Giovanni.

A digital photograph depicts "Visione dell'aldilà, la caduta dei dannati" by Hieronymus Bosch. The photograph was taken by Alessia Polesel and is part of the collection "bhex-polesel-2012-51-52-53-dvd1-55". The photograph was taken on March 25, 2013, using a flash, and is in color. Copyright for the image is held by Rodolfo Polesel and is restricted.

The painting "Fall of the Damned" by Hieronymus Bosch is located in the Doge's Palace in Venice. It is part of a cycle of four depictions of the afterlife, created between 1500 and 1504. The oil painting on wood depicts hell and measures 88.5 x 41.5 cm. It is cataloged in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome under the signature T,001.

The cycle includes three other paintings: "Hell", "Ascent of the Saved into Paradise", and "The Heavenly Paradise". All four works are also oil paintings on wood and have the same dimensions of 88.5 x 41.5 cm. They are also cataloged in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome under the signatures T,002 to T,004.
A scan of an unknown image from the collection bhex-pommersfelden-schoenborn-1719-55 was made on May 23, 2007. The photograph is a color print on Ektachrome and comes from a restricted loan.

The painting, which was once in the private collection of Pommersfelden, was acquired by Count Schönborn before 1719. The second previous owner was an unknown man from Rome who owned the work around 1700. Previously, the painting was mistakenly attributed to Annibale Carracci.

The 1719 catalogue of the Pommersfelden collection classified the painting as Roman and dated it to 1601/1700. It is a copy after the painting "John the Baptist" by Michelangelo Merisi da Caravaggio, which is in the Pinacoteca Capitolina in Rome. The work itself is 139 x 101 cm in size and is also documented in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.

The property manager in Pommersfelden manages a private collection. The collection consists of 55 objects and dates back to before 1719. The first owner was Schönborn, probably a count. The second owner was unknown in Rome around 1700.

A digital photograph, part of the Bibliotheca Hertziana, with the number P0021832_CC.tif, shows a full view of a work of art. The photograph was taken on July 8, 2024, by Enrico Fontolan and shows the artwork unframed, along with a Color Checker.  Release for publication was granted on November 21, 2024. 

The image is in color and was published on July 20, 2024.

The landscape painter Achille Vertunni created the painting "The Landscape around Salerno" in 1885. The work, an oil painting on canvas, depicts the landscape around Salerno in Italy. The dimensions of the painting are 100 x 200 cm. The painting is in the possession of the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna in Rome and was acquired in 1895. The artist's signature, "A. Vertunni 1885", is located in the lower right corner. 

The publication "Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna. Le collezioni. Il XIX secolo" by E. di Majo and M. Lafranconi from 2006 mentions the painting on page 256, catalogue number 9.15.
The curator of the Rome Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna is responsible for the acquisition of artworks. In 1895, he acquired an object designated "OBJ".

A digital photograph of the Bibliotheca Hertziana, with the file number P0021834a.tif, was uploaded by bhim00055760 on November 22, 2024. It depicts an artwork with the number 2024.11.22. The photograph was taken by Enrico Fontolan on July 8, 2024. It shows a full view of the artwork without a frame. The photograph has been released.

The painter Giovanni Carnovali created the portrait of a writing man around 1840/1843. The painting, an oil painting on canvas, depicts the man in the act of writing and measures 75 x 60.5 cm. The work was purchased in 1940 by the curator of the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna. Its origin before the purchase is unknown; it was previously in a private collection of Francesco Marchionni.

The portrait is part of the collection of the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna in Rome and was documented in the publication "Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna. Le collezioni. Il XIX secolo" edited by E. di Majo and M. Lafranconi in 2006.

The custodian of the object is the Rom Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna. The object was acquired in 1940. Prior to that, it was part of a private collection of Marchionni, Francesco, the previous owner of which is unknown.

A digital photograph from the Bibliotheca Hertziana, with the number bhim00037165.tif, was released as HER0359a.tif on October 29, 2018. The photograph shows a full view of a work of art by Enrico Fontolan, taken during the photo campaign 24/2018. The image is in color and was taken without a frame.

The painting "Hagar and the Angel" was created in Rome in 1776 by Pompeo Girolamo Batoni. The oil painting on canvas measures 100 x 151.5 cm and is in the possession of the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica in the Palazzo Barberini. The work is signed: "1776 Pompeo De Batoni / P. Romae 1776" on the lower right corner of the picture on a rock.

The illustration depicts the biblical scene of Hagar and the angel who comforts her.
The administrator of the property is the Rom Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica, located at Palazzo Barberini, address 2374, 1953.

A digital photograph from the Bibliotheca Hertziana, with the image number bhim00037168, is saved as HER0372.tif. The photograph, taken on October 29, 2018, shows a full view of a work of art by Enrico Fontolan. The photograph is from the photo campaign 25/2018 and was released on October 29, 2018. The image is in color.

The architectural fantasy featuring ancient ruins dates from 1712 and was created by Francesco Guardi. The painting, an oil painting on canvas, depicts a scene with ancient ruins in an architectural setting. The work measures 43 x 35 cm and is in the possession of the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica Palazzo Barberini in Rome.

The painting was described in the catalogue "Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica. Palazzo Barberini, i dipinti. Catalogo sistematico" by L. Mochi Onori and R. Vodret (eds.) from 2008. It is located in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.
The administrator of the Rom Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica is the Palazzo Barberini, located at address 2484.

A digital photograph of the Bibliotheca Hertziana with the image number bhim00037172.tif and the internal designation HER0378.tif was taken on October 30, 2018. The photograph shows a work of art by Enrico Fontolan, which is part of the photo campaign 25/2018. It is a full view of the artwork without a frame. The photograph is in color and was released on August 8, 2018.

The painting "View of Procuratie Vecchie Venice" was painted by Giovanni Antonio Canaletto (1697-1768) around 1750. It depicts Piazza San Marco to the southwest, overlooking the Church of San Geminiano and the Procuratie Vecchie. The oil painting on canvas measures 68.5 x 93.5 cm and is located in the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica Palazzo Barberini in Rome.  

The depiction shows the Procuratie Vecchie, the Procuratie Nuove, the Church of San Geminiano, Piazza San Marco, the Torre dell'Orologio, the Loggetta, and the Campanile di San Marco. The painting was documented by L. Mochi Onori and R. Vodret in the catalog "Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica. Palazzo Barberini, i dipinti" (Rome 2008).
The administrator of the property is the Rom Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica in the Palazzo Barberini, with the address 1061.

A digital photograph of the Bibliotheca Hertziana, designated "bhim00037173.tif", was taken on October 30, 2018, under the number HER0379.tif. The photograph depicts a work of art released in 2018 and captured on August 25, 2018, by Enrico Fontolan as part of a photo campaign. It is a full view with frame. 

The photograph is in color and is titled "art".

The painting "View of Procuratie Vecchie, Venice" was created by Giovanni Antonio Canal, better known as Canaletto, around 1697. It depicts Piazza San Marco facing southwest, towards San Geminiano and the Procuratie. The oil painting on canvas measures 68.5 x 93.5 cm.

The view includes the Procuratie Vecchie, the Procuratie Nuove, the Church of San Geminiano, Piazza San Marco, the Torre dell'Orologio, the Loggetta, and the Campanile di San Marco. The work is in the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica in the Palazzo Barberini in Rome and was described by L. Mochi Onori and R. Vodret in the catalogue "Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica. Palazzo Barberini, i dipinti. Catalogo sistematico" of 2008.
The administrator of the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica in Rome is Palazzo Barberini 1061.

A digital photograph of Roberto Sigismondi from 1381.201.tif was taken on July 6, 2023, with the designation "bhex-2022-35-203 art".  Release for the full view with frame was granted for the artist Roberto Sigismondi. The order number is 35/2022 and the rights are divided. The photograph is in color.

The administrator of the Gubbio Palazzo Ducale was once the Gubbio Comune di Gubbio. Formerly, the administrator of the Gubbio Palazzo dei Consoli was, and today the Museo Civico houses the Pinacoteca. The painting "The Pentecost Miracle" was created by Benedetto Nucci or an artist from his circle. It was created in 1566 and is an oil painting on canvas. The painting measures 122 x 91 cm and shows signs of paint loss.

On the step of the throne, there is an inscription with the words "1566.Sa. B. D. S. L. / M.D. LXVI." The Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome has documentation of the painting.
The property manager is Gubbio Palazzo Ducale. The owner is Gubbio Comune di Gubbio 254. Previously, Gubbio Museo Civico Palazzo dei Consoli Pinacoteca 5866 was the property manager's depot.

A digital photograph of the Bibliotheca Hertziana with the image number bhim00037056.tif. The photograph is titled "art 2018.10.16 HER0156" and was taken on October 16, 2018. It is a color photograph showing a full view by Enrico Fontolan.  Release for publication was granted on August 8, 2018.

The painter Domenico Zampieri, known as Domenichino, created the oil painting "Throned Madonna with Saints John the Evangelist and Petronius." The painting, measuring 430 x 278 cm, has been in the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica in the Palazzo Barberini in Rome since 1992. Prior to that, it was housed in the Pinacoteca di Brera in Milan from 1812 to 1953. The painting originated in the church of Santi Giovanni Evangelista e Petronio dei Bolognesi in Rome, where it was temporarily kept. From 1953 to 1992, it was located in the Circolo Ufficiali delle Forze Armate club in Rome.
The curator of the Rom Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica Palazzo Barberini served from 1992 to 2074. Prior to that, the curator was based in Milan at the Pinacoteca di Brera from 1812 to 1953.

A digital photograph of the artwork "Simone Martini" from the O.C.S.A. Museo Civico in Altomonte (CS) is available. The photograph was taken on June 10, 2020, and is designated "bhex-2020-06-109 art 2020.06.11". The color scheme was established by Marcello Leotta in 2019. The photograph was ordered in June 2020 and the overall view was approved.

The painting "Saint Ladislaus of Hungary" was created between 1326 and 1328 by Simone di Martino. The work, a tempera painting on wood, depicts Saint Ladislaus of Hungary. The painting measures 45.5x21.5 cm.  On the underside of the painting is the inscription "S. LADISLAUS/ REX UNGARIE". 

The painting is part of the collection of the Altomonte Museo Civico di Santa Maria della Consolazione. It was first presented in the publication "Santa Maria della Consolazione ad Altomonte. Un cantiere gotico in Calabria" by Stefania Paone (Rome 2014).
The property manager is the Altomonte Museo Civico di Santa Maria della Consolazione.

A digital photograph of the Bibliotheca Hertziana, designated bhim00039606.tif, taken on May 30, 2022, shows a detail of the frame of a painting. The painting itself is titled "The Capture of Christ" and originates from Roberto Sigismondi's photo campaign 12/2019.

The photograph is in color and has been released for use.

In Rome, in the Palazzo della Valle, on the noble floor, there is a hall with the impressive Sala delle Sibille. The coffered ceiling of this hall is adorned with depictions of the Sibylles. Francesco Salviati or an artist from his circle is suspected as the author of this ceiling painting. The work was created between 1523 and 1550. The ceiling is made of wood and painted.

The Sala delle Sibille houses four paintings depicting the Cumean, Erythraean, Persian, and European Sibylles. These paintings are in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome and were first published in 2022.

A digital photograph of the Bibliotheca Hertziana (bhim00039604) shows a detailed view of the frame of a painting. The painting, depicting the Entry of Christ into Jerusalem, was photographed by Roberto Sigismondi in January 2019 as part of a photography campaign. The photograph was released in color on May 30, 2022.

In the Palazzo della Valle in Rome, on the noble floor, is the Sala delle Sibille. The coffered ceiling of this room is adorned with depictions of the Sibylles. The ceiling is attributed to Francesco Salviati and was probably created between 1523 and 1550. 

The ceiling consists of painted wooden panels and depicts four Sibylles: the Cumaean, the Erythraean, the Persian, and the European Sibylle. These paintings were documented by the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.

A digital photograph from the Hertziana Library (image number bhim00039607.tif), taken in 2019 as part of the photo campaign 12/2019. The photograph shows a close-up view of the depiction "The Massacre of the Innocents" and was created by Roberto Sigismondi. It was released on May 30, 2022. The image is in color.

In the Palazzo della Valle in Rome, on the piano nobile, there is a hall with a remarkable coffered ceiling, known as the Sala delle Sibille. The ceiling is adorned with depictions of the Sibylles and is attributed to Francesco Salviati. The painting of the wooden ceiling dates from the period between 1523 and 1550.

The ceiling shows four depictions of Sibylles: the Cumean Sibyl, the Erythraean Sibyl, the Persian Sibyl, and the European Sibyl. These paintings are in the possession of the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome and have been documented there.

A digital photograph of Paolo di Ciacio, from the O.C.S.A. Museo Civico in Altomonte (CS), was archived as "bhex-2020-06-113 art 2020.06.11". The photograph is a color image by Marcello Leotta from 2019 and was ordered in June 2020. It is an overall view that has been released.

The painting "Madonna with Pears" (also known as "Madonna delle pere") was painted by Paolo di Ciacio di Mileto and is today located in the Altomonte Museo Civico di Santa Maria della Consolazione. The work was created on a walnut wood panel and depicts the Madonna with pears, painted in oil on walnut wood. The dimensions of the painting are 85 x 65 cm. It was restored in 1972 and 2014.
The property manager is the Altomonte Museo Civico di Santa Maria della Consolazione.

The Staatsgalerie Stuttgart holds a digital photograph, cataloged under the number sgs_mup_panini_3315_B.tif. The photograph was inventoried in 2014 under the designation bhex-st-2014-30-1. The image dates to November 12, 2014, and bears the inventory number art 2014.11.12. The photograph is in color and was ordered on August 6, 2007. The order number is 30/2014. Currently, the photograph is restricted.

The Staatsgalerie Stuttgart houses the painting "Roma Moderna" by Giovanni Paolo Pannini. The work was created between 1754 and 1757 on commission from Duc Choiseul, Étienne-François de Choiseul. The oil painting on canvas depicts a view of modern Rome and measures 169 x 227 cm. 

The painting is part of a series that also includes a pendant "Roma Antica" by Giovanni Paolo Pannini. The two works are now in the Boston Museum of Fine Arts and the Staatsgalerie Stuttgart.
The administrator of the Staatsgalerie Stuttgart is the Stuttgart Administrator.

A photograph of unknown origin depicts a rare species from the years 1940 to 1944. It is an albumen print, fully mounted and slightly faded. The back bears a Fox stamp. On the front are two cards stuck together.

The painting "Prayer of Christ in the Garden of Gethsemane" was made by Marcello Venusti and is part of the Galleria Doria Pamphilj in Rome. It is an oil painting on wood. The dimensions of the painting are 58 x 82.3 cm. The work is located in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.
The manager of the Galleria Doria Pamphilj is in Rome.

A digital photograph of Roberto Sigismondi from 1392.59.tif was colorized on July 7, 2023, under the designation bhex-2022-23-084. The photograph was ordered by Roberto Sigismondi on April 17, 2023, and is part of order 23/2022. The usage rights are divided, and permission for the full view has been granted.

In the church of San Pietro in Gubbio, on the right, southern wall of the first side chapel, there is a painting of Saint Francis of Assisi. The work is by Rutilio di Lorenzo Manetti and was created between 1601 and 1639. It is an oil painting measuring 180 x 83 cm. 


Information about the painting comes from the source "Prospettiva", July 1985, issue 42, pages 65-67. The author of the article is Enzo Storelli, who deals with Rutilio Manetti and his works in Gubbio.

A digital photograph of Roberto Sigismondi from 1392.58.tif, designated bhex-2022-23-083, was digitized in color on July 7, 2023. Roberto Sigismondi ordered the photograph on April 17, 2023. The order number was 23/2022. The rights to the photograph are divided. The full view has been released.

The first side chapel on the right, southern wall of the church of San Pietro in Gubbio houses a painting of Saint Onuphrius. The work was created by Rutilio di Lorenzo Manetti and dates from between 1601 and 1639. The oil painting, measuring 180 x 83 cm, depicts Saint Onuphrius in a detailed style. 

The research and documentation of this painting was driven by Enzo Storelli. Storelli published his findings in the journal "Prospettiva" in 1985, where he also presented the unknown works of Manetti in Gubbio.
A photograph from the Alinari Archive, taken in France before 1957. It is a rare black and white photograph on silver gelatin. The photograph is in good condition and shows no stamps.

The painting "Madonna del coniglio" comes from the workshop of the famous Italian painter Titian, who was also known as Tiziano, Titian, Tiziano Vecelio, or Tiziano Vecelio. It was created around the year 1530 and is an oil painting on canvas measuring 74 x 84 cm. The work bears the signature "TICIANVS". The provenance of the painting is documented in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.
The curator of the Paris Musée National du Louvre, Department of Painting, is named Curator Paris Musée National du Louvre Department of Painting 743.

A photograph from Marburg, taken on April 3, 2000. It shows a family chapel, photographed by Gloc as part of a KHI photo campaign in 2000. The photo campaign documented a total of 200 family chapels. The photograph is in black and white and was taken with a camera. The image shows a general view of the chapel, which is closed. 

The image is numbered B 27.231/2 tosc xart and is part of the Museum Foto Marburg collection.

The altar is located in the church of Santa Maria in Gradi in Arezzo and was made around 1654 by Santini, Bernardino di Bartolommeo. The altarpiece depicts the Holy Family with Saint Benedict. The third altar on the right is an oil painting on canvas.

The left side of the altarpiece shows the dream of Saint Joseph, the right side the destruction of pagan idols by Saint Benedict. Another painting on the altar depicts angels with episcopal insignia.

A digital photograph of the Bibliotheca Hertziana with the file ID bhim00027604.tif. It was sighted on August 11, 2016, and is in color. The photograph shows a full view of a work by Roberto Sigismondi, released in 2015.

The painting "Rosalia and Maria pray before the Trinity for Ciminna" was created in 1627/1628. It was painted by Geronimo Gerardi and is located in the Chiesa Madre Santa Maria Maddalena church in Ciminna. The oil painting depicts the saints Rosalia and Maria praying before the Trinity for Ciminna. The work is painted on canvas and measures 275 x 199 cm. 


Geronimo Gerardi, the artist of the painting, is listed in the Allgemeines Künstlerlexicon (AKL) under the number akl_41008557. The painting was mentioned in the publication "Pompa Magna, Piana degli Albanesi 2008" by G. Davì and G. Mendola and is located in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.
A photograph from the Archivio dell'Arte archive, number PV0076, shows the work "bhex-pedicini-pv0076" by Luciano Pedicini. The photograph was taken on November 29, 2007.

The painter François de Nomé created the painting "Conversion of Saint Paul". The work is an oil painting on canvas. The dimensions of the painting are 73 cm in height and 22 cm in width. It is in the private collection of a manager from Naples. Previously, it was in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.
The curator of the Naples Collection is private.

A photograph from the Central Collecting Point Munich (CCP) is numbered CP131440 and is part of the rare exhibition "raro-art" in 2024. It is a black and white silver gelatin print from the estate of the artist Johannes Felbermeyer. The estate was received in 1997. Wolfgang Lotz has designated the photograph as "Loose Photograph Rs. hs.". On the back is the inscription "Rembrandt, Self-Portrait ex Rathenau Fot CCP CCP Mü-Nr. 1416/1".

The photograph shows a full view of the print and is recorded with the dimensions 17.2 x 12 cm.

Rembrandt van Rijn's self-portrait from 1669 is in the possession of the Mauritshuis in The Hague. The painting, an oil painting on canvas, depicts the artist himself and measures 63.5 x 57.8 cm. It was previously owned by Ernest G. Rathenau in Berlin, Ettlinger. Christian Tümpel mentions the work in his book "Rembrandt: all paintings in colour" published in 1993.

The administrator of the object is the Koninklijk Kabinet van Schilderijen Mauritshuis in The Hague. The artwork is in its possession in the collection. The previous owner was Ernest G. Rathenau from Ettlingen, Berlin.

This is a photograph of unknown origin. It was likely produced between 1940 and 1944 and is a black and white photograph on silver gelatin. There are indications of a possible connection to the artist Faraglia, but this has not yet been confirmed. The photograph was part of a gift from Hermann and Jane, and it has been released for further use.

The painter Salvator Rosa created the painting "Allegory of Music" as an oil painting on canvas. The work was purchased in 1932 by Guido Tavazzi, the administrator of the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica in Rome. The purchase took place in December 1932 through a dealer in Rome. Previously, the painting was in the private collection of the Rospigliosi family in Rome. The painting measures 71 x 60 cm and bears the signature "[...] Rosa" at the end of the musical score. 

"Allegory of Music" is part of the collection of the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica in the Palazzo Barberini in Rome. It was mentioned in the 2008 catalog "Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica. Palazzo Barberini, i dipinti. Catalogo sistematico" by L. Mochi Onori and R. Vodret. Further information about the painting is available at the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.

The curator of the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica in the Palazzo Barberini in Rome was responsible for the purchase of the object in 1932. The intermediary for the purchase was Guido Tavazzi from Rome, who facilitated the sale between December 12th and 24th, 1932. Prior to that, the object was in the private collection of the Rospigliosi family in Rome.

A digital photograph from the Bibliotheca Hertziana, with the image number bhim00027611. The photograph was scanned on August 12, 2016, and is in color. It shows a full view of a work by Roberto Sigismondi and was released in 2015.

The painting "Christus übergibt Petrus die Schlüssel und Befreiung Petri" is a work by the artist Vincenzo Barbera, dating from 1629. The oil painting on canvas measures 73 cm in height and 71 cm in width. The painting depicts the scene in which Christ gives Peter the keys, thereby granting him freedom. The artwork is located in the Chiesa Madre Santa Maria Maddalena church in Ciminna. 

Vincenzo Barbera is also known as La Barbera, Vincenzio Barbera, Vincenzo da Barbera, or Vincenzo la.

A rare photo of Alinari Anderson from the years 1940 to 1944. It is an albumen print measuring 576 mm and is fully adhered. The photo shows creases and a tear at the left edge. On the back is a stamp and two Ks., stuck on top of each other.

The painting "The Resurrection of Lazarus" was created by Leandro Bassano between 1592 and 1596 in Bassano del Grappa. The work is now in the Galleria dell'Accademia in Venice. The panel painting depicts the scene of the resurrection of Lazarus and is 410 x 238 cm in size. In the lower center of the painting is the signature "LEANDER / BASSANE / F.".

Another indication of the artist is the inscription "LEANDER / BASSANE / F.", which is also located in the lower center of the painting. The scientific research of the painting was advanced among others by Moschini and Marconi. The Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome possesses relevant documents concerning the work.
The manager of the Venice Galleria dell'Accademia 320 is the Galleria dell'Accademia.

A digital photograph of the Bibliotheca Hertziana, identified as bhim00037029.tif and bhim00037029. It is part of the "art" collection and was taken on October 15, 2018, under the designation HER0111.tif. The photograph is in color and shows a full view with frame of the work by Enrico Fontolan, released in August 2018.

The painting "The Last Supper" was made by Valentin de Boulogne around 1620. It is in the possession of the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica in Rome, which displays it in the Palazzo Barberini. The oil painting on canvas measures 175.5 x 256 cm and is part of the Mattei Collection. The artwork was documented by L. Mochi Onori and R. Vodret in the catalogue "Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica. Palazzo Barberini, i dipinti. Catalogo sistematico" from 2008.
The administrator of the Rom Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica is Palazzo Barberini 1362.

A digital photograph, part of the collection of the O.C.S.A. Museo Civico in Altomonte (CS), depicts an altarolo with the forms of a released form. The photograph, taken on June 12, 2020, bears the number 34 and was commissioned by Marcello Leotta in 2019.

The overall view of the altarolo was released on June 12, 2020, and is part of collection number 8, item 2020.06.12.

The triptych with scenes from the Passion of Christ originates from Altomonte and was created between 1401 and 1410. It is currently located in the Museo Civico di Santa Maria della Consolazione in Altomonte. The work was executed by a master associated with Antonio and Onofrio Penna, in the technique of panel painting. The triptych is an altarpiece painted on wood in tempera. It consists of three parts that can be closed. The overall dimensions of the triptych are 183 x 117. The Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome has detailed records of individual parts of the triptych. The individual paintings include: The Kiss of Judas, Christ before Anne, Christ before the High Council, Christ before Pontius Pilate, Christ before Herod, Christ is whipped by soldiers, Crowning with Thorns, Carrying the Cross, Crucifixion of Christ, Lamentation of Christ, and Resurrection of Christ.
The property manager is the Altomonte Museo Civico di Santa Maria della Consolazione.

A coal print by Braun, Ad., et Cie. from Dornach dates from 1965. The etching is titled "raro-art" and has been approved. A sticker stamp is attached to the edge of the artwork in very good condition.

The painting "Toilette of Venus" is on display at the Musée National du Louvre in Paris. The work is attributed to Francesco Albani, who lived around 1578. The painting is an oil on canvas and measures 202 x 252 cm. The Hertziana Library in Rome owns a copy of the work.
The administrator of the Paris Musée National du Louvre is the Paris Musée National du Louvre.

A digital photograph of the Bibliotheca Hertziana, with image number bhim00037039.tif and internal designation HER0134.tif, dates from 2018. It shows a full view of an artwork by Enrico Fontolan, taken on October 15, 2018. The photograph is in color and shows the artwork with its frame. Permission for the use of the photograph was granted in August 2018.

The painting "John the Baptist" by Pier Francesco Mola was acquired in 1762 by the administrator Rom of the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica Palazzo Barberini and remained in his possession until 1918. It is an oil painting on canvas measuring 99 x 133 cm.

The depiction shows Christ pointing to John the Baptist. The work is part of the collection of the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica, Palazzo Barberini in Rome and was documented in the catalogue "Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica. Palazzo Barberini, i dipinti. Catalogo sistematico" by L. Mochi Onori and R. Vodret (eds.) from 2008 on page 287.
The administrator of the Rome Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica was the Palazzo Barberini from 1762 to 1918.

A slide of unknown origin depicts a 1992 Ferrari. The image was shot in Ektachrome color and is part of Volume 1, Plate XVI of the work "Dono Ferrari, Oreste". The slide measures 10 x 12.5 cm and is sealed.

Luca Giordano, former curator of the public collection in Naples, painted the painting "Apollo and Marsyas" in 1659/1660. It is an oil painting on canvas, measuring 205×259 cm. The work is in the Museo e Gallerie Nazionali di Capodimonte in Naples. 

The art historical literature on Luca Giordano mentions the painting under the catalogue number A 128 in the first volume of the publication "Luca Giordano - L'opera completa" by O. Ferrari and G. Scavizzi from 1992. The work is also documented in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.

The former curator of the Neapolitan public collection Museo Nazionale di San Martino worked in Naples. He is currently the curator of the Neapolitan public collection Museo e Gallerie Nazionali di Capodimonte.

A digital photograph of Ventura, Domenico titled "001_DSC7238.tif" and with the file name "bhex-2020-24-004". It was taken in color on June 8, 2021. The photograph was commissioned by Ventura, Domenico in 2018 and belongs to the Fototeca Unione. The rights to the image are divided. The photograph shows the overall view of an object after restoration and is released.

The painting "Saint Catherine of Alexandria" was created between 1601 and 1650. It originates from the church of Santo Stefano in Bracciano, Latium. The anonymous artist painted the picture on canvas with oil. The work is in the possession of the Museo dell'Opera del Duomo di Bracciano.
The administrator of the Bracciano Museo dell'Opera del Duomo di Bracciano is Bracciano.

A digital photograph of Ventura, Domenico titled 003_DSC7256.tif was digitized on June 8, 2021, with the identifier "bhex-2020-24-012". The detail shows a landscape that is released.

The painting "Saint Catherine of Alexandria" is from the workshop of an unknown artist dating from between 1601 and 1650. The oil painting on canvas was painted in the church of Santo Stefano in Bracciano, Latium. 

It is now in the collection of the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome and was recorded there on June 8, 2021. The administrator of the Bracciano Museo dell'Opera del Duomo di Bracciano was responsible for the entry into the database.
The administrator of the Bracciano Museo dell'Opera del Duomo di Bracciano is Bracciano.

A rare photograph of Alinari Anderson from between 1940 and 1944 is preserved in this albumen print. The photograph is fully adhered and shows traces of fading, foxing, and stains caused by an ink cartridge. It is underlined with two Ks stuck together. On the back there is an overwriting in pencil and ink.

On the back there is also a stamp with foxing and the initials "Rs."

The curator of the Museo del Prado in Madrid has released the painting "Portrait of a Young Woman". The work is by the painter Nicolò dell'Abate. The oil painting on canvas measures 64 x 50 cm. It was part of the 1969 exhibition "Mostra di Nicolò dell'Abate", curated by S.M. Beguin. 

The exhibition was held at the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome. The painting is mentioned in the catalogue on pages 64-65, under number 17.
The property manager is the Museo del Prado in Madrid. The address is 416.

This is a rare photograph of Alinari Anderson from before 1957. It is an albumen print, released in detail. The photograph is fully mounted and shows slight toning on the surface as well as slight spots. On the back there is an inscription in ballpoint pen that reads "Vs.". There is no stamp.

The painting "Saint Catherine of Alexandria" was created by Giovanni d'Alemagna. The work was created around 1441 and is an oil painting on wood. The work is in the possession of the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome and bears the signature "cfi" there.

Giovanni d'Alemagna is also known under various other names, including Giovanni de, Alamagna, Giovanni Todesco, Giovanni Teutonico, Johanes Alamanus, Alamanus, Johanes, Iohannes de Alemania, Iohannes de Muriano, Zoanne Alamanus, Alamanus, Zoanne, Zuane da Murano, Zuane de Muriano and Zuanne Todesco.
The manager of the Venice Gallerie dell'Accademia is the Venice Manager.

A photograph from the raro-art museum dating back to 1966, as a charcoal print, is released. It has been repeatedly glued to the edge, causing it to bend. There is a crack in the upper left corner. The photograph is pencil-inscribed. It is inscribed with ink, ballpoint pen, and pencil. The attribution was confirmed by Pepper. A stamp is affixed to the photograph.

In 1578, the painter Francesco Albani created the painting "Annunciation of the Virgin". The work is in the possession of the Musée National du Louvre in Paris and was published by Albani's administrator. The oil painting on canvas measures 73 cm in height and 52 cm in width.  

The painting is archived in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome and is listed under the designation "cfi".
The administrator of the Paris Musée National du Louvre is the Paris Musée National du Louvre.

This is a digital photograph, stored as a tif file by the Bibliotheca Hertziana under the record ID bhim00052578. The photograph is titled "chi" and was taken on May 11, 2023. It is in color and shows a general view of a work by Enrico Fontolan. The photograph was taken on January 25, 2023 as part of a 2023 photo campaign and is released.

The painting "Saint Mary Magdalene and Saint Martha" is located in the Cappella del Crocifisso on the right side wall of the third chapel to the left of the octagon in the Santa Maria della Pace church in Rome. It was made between 1551 and 1600 by Ventura Salimbeni and Bevilacqua Maler. The pendant to the painting is in the work of Jacopo Zucchi.

The depiction is rectangular and oil on canvas. The painting is mentioned in "Roma Sacra. Guida alle chiese della città eterna, Itinerario 11, Naples/Rome 1997" by Maria Pia D'Orazio. Further information can be found in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.

A digital photograph from the Hertziana Library (bhim00036630.tif, bhim00036630 Oratorio-SS-Rosario--32.tif) shows the overall view of the Oratorio-SS-Rosario. The photograph was taken in color on September 25, 2018, by Roberto Sigismondi as part of campaign 28/2018. It was released for the 2018 study course.

A painting of the Crowning with Thorns of Christ is located on the right wall of the nave of the Oratorio del Rosario di San Domenico in Palermo. The oil painting on canvas is Flemish and dates from 1601 to 1650. 

The painting was mentioned by P. Palazzotto in his publication "Palermo: guida agli oratori" from 2004 and in "Giacomo Serpotta: gli oratori di Palermo, guida storico-artistica" from 2016. The dimensions of the painting are 73 D x 35 2.

A digital photograph of the Bibliotheca Hertziana with the capture ID bhim00035173.tif. It is part of the "art" collection and was taken on January 11, 2018. The capture was registered under number HER8561a and is in color. The photograph depicts the work of Enrico Fontolan and was taken from October 12 to 27, 2017 as part of the photo campaign 26/2017. The photograph is unframed and has been released.

The painting "The Reading Saint Jerome" was created in the workshop of Guido Reni. The work, an oil painting on canvas, depicts the saint Jerome reading and measures 77 x 65 cm. It is housed in the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica Palazzo Corsini in Rome, which is managed by the Galleria's administrator in Rome.
The administrator of the Rom Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica is Palazzo Corsini 482 Galleria del Cardinale.

A digital photograph of the Bibliotheca Hertziana, labeled bhim00035172.tif, dates from 2018. It depicts the artwork HER8561, photographed by Enrico Fontolan. The photograph was taken during the photo campaign 26/2017 between October 12th and 27th, 2017. The photo was taken with a color filter and shows the artwork with its frame.

The Reading Saint Jerome is a painting by the Italian painter Guido Reni. The work was created during the Baroque period and is now in the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica Palazzo Corsini in Rome. The oil painting on canvas depicts the Saint Jerome reading and measures 77 x 65 cm.
The administrator of the property is the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica Palazzo Corsini, located in Rome. The address is Palazzo Corsini 482 Galleria del Cardinale.

A photograph of unknown origin shows a rare item from the years 1940 to 1944. It is an albumen print, completely glued to the left side. In one place, the print is torn and shows slight toning. On the back are two small photographs glued together. 

The back of the photograph also has adhesive marks and a stamp.

The "Madonna with Two Angels" is a painting by the artist Andrea Previtali, cataloged by Heinemann in 1962. It is an expanded copy of Boccaccino's work, Boccaccio, from 1466. The painting was originally transferred to wood, but later to canvas. It measures 67.3 x 92.7 cm and is part of the collection of the Kunsthistorisches Institut in Florence Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.  

A double recording of the "Madonna with Two Angels" is found in the collection of the National Gallery in London. The painting was made by Andrea Previtali from Cordeliaghi. Further information about this work can be found in the publications of Meyer zur Capellen (1972), Chiappini (1975).
The curator of the London National Gallery is the curator London National Gallery 3111.

A photograph from the Sopran Gallery in Naples, taken on January 8, 2008. The photograph is in black and white and was donated as a gift by Oreste Ferrari. Access to this photograph is currently restricted.

The Rosary Madonna with Saint Dominic and Saint Catherine of Siena was painted by Luca Giordano around 1686. The painting is an oil on canvas measuring 430 x 240 cm. It is in the collection of the Museo e Gallerie Nazionali di Capodimonte in Naples. The work was created by Giordano for the administrator of the museum in Naples.
The administrator of the Naples Museum and the National Galleries Capodimonte is the Naples Museo e Gallerie Nazionali di Capodimonte.
A photograph from the collection of the Sopr. Gall. Napoli, dated January 8, 2008. The black-and-white photograph shows a detail that is closed off. It was donated by Dono Ferrari, Oreste.

Luca Giordano painted the Rosary Madonna with Saint Dominic and Saint Catherine of Siena. The painting was created around 1686 and is an oil painting on canvas measuring 430 x 240 cm. The depiction shows the Madonna with the Rosary, Saint Dominic, and Saint Catherine of Siena. The work is in the collection of the Museo e Gallerie Nazionali di Capodimonte in Naples and was documented by O. Ferrari and G. Scavizzi in their work "Luca Giordano - L'opera completa, Vol. 1" (Naples 1992).
The administrator of the Naples Museo e Gallerie Nazionali di Capodimonte is Naples.

A rare Alinari photograph from between 1953 and 1956 is preserved as a charcoal print. The print is numbered 277 and is fully adhered. It is slightly scratched at the edges. There is a stain on the front, and on the back there are paper scraps and traces of writing from a previous use. A stamp is also present.

The Milan curators of the Museo d'Arte Antica published a painting signed "Bellini, Giovanni (1430) attributed to". It is a panel painting, described as "Portrait of a Humanist" and executed in oil on wood. The dimensions of the painting are 35 x 28 cm. There is an alternative attribution to Antonello da Messina. 

The painting is part of the collection of the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome. It has been mentioned in various publications, including "Heinemann, 1962 Vol. 1, Cat. V. 110" and "Fiorio-Garberi, Catalogue, 1987".
The curator of the Milan Museo d'Arte Antica is Curator Milan Museo d'Arte Antica 249.
A photograph from the Réunion des Musées Nationaux collection shows a black-and-white overall view of an artwork from the 1980s. The image is restricted.

The Crucifixion originated in Florence in the Cappella Antinori chapel of the Santo Spirito church. Until 1813, the painting was located in Florence. Subsequently, it came into the possession of the Paris Musée National du Louvre. The oil painting on wood, measuring 195 x 191 cm, was probably created between 1496 and 1505 by Biagio d'Antonio Tucci.

Earlier, the work was also attributed to Bertucci, Giovan Battista, and later to Ghirlandaio, Benedetto.

The attribution to Biagio d'Antonio was confirmed by art historian Berenson in 1932.

The Crucifixion is part of the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome and was mentioned in the publication "Biagio d'Antonio, Milan 1999" by R. Bartoli.
The administrator of the Paris Musée National du Louvre is the Paris Musée National du Louvre 296.

A photograph of the Bibliotheca Hertziana U.Pl. with the image number bhpd49450 shows two Caryatids that are closed. The photograph was taken on November 11, 1997, and is in the possession of Savio, Oscar. Reproduction is permitted by Conte Novello Cavazza.

The ceiling painting "Aurora and Phosphorus" is located in the Palazzo Borghese in Rome, on the second floor, in the wing facing Piazza (D 25). The work dates from around 1740/1750 and was created by Antonio Bicchierai. The oval ceiling painting is executed in tempera on canvas and depicts ancient mythology. It is part of a fictional architectural frame decorated with caryatids, putti, and a cycle of oval paintings with mythological scenes. 

Other ceiling paintings in the same room depict scenes from Greek mythology. One of the ceiling paintings depicts the abduction of Europa by the bull.

A photograph of unknown origin, classified as a rarity, was produced as a silver gelatin print between 1953 and 1956. The photograph is completely mounted and heavily faded. It exhibits toning and has cracks. In addition, there are paper remnants and markings on the photograph that suggest prior use. There is no stamp.

The "Lamentation of Christ" is a painting attributed to the painter Orazio Gentileschi. The painting is in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome. The work is 73 cm high and 72 cm wide. The date of creation of the painting is unknown.
The manager is unknown.

The photograph is copyrighted and belongs to N. M. dem König from 1971. It is a charcoal print that is sealed. A sticker has been attached to the edge, which is in good condition. The marking on the stamp reads "c art".

The semi-public collection at Kensington Palace houses a painting by Artemisia Gentileschi. The work, La Pittura (Self-Portrait as an Allegory of Painting), is an oil painting on canvas measuring 97 x 74 cm. The painting was created by Gentileschi and is part of the Stolzenwald collection.

A photograph of the painting is held in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.
The curator of the semi-public collection at Kensington Palace is located in London.

A charcoal drawing by Braun, Ad., et Cie., Dornach from the years 1953 to 1956 is shown in this photograph. The artwork is titled "raro-art" and was created in 1953/1956. On the back are two Ks., glued together, along with inscriptions and paper scraps that suggest previous use. A stamp is also present.

The Madonna Benson is a panel painting by Antonello da Messina. It was published by the Washington National Gallery of Art and was previously owned by Robert H. Benson. The painting was made by Antonello da Messina, who is also known as Antonello de Antonio, Antonio de Antonio, Antonello di Giovanni, Antonius de Messana, Antonellus de Antonio, Antonellus messanesis, Antonellus messaneus, Antonellus messanus, Antonellus siculus, Antonj, Antonello degli Antonj, Antonius degli Antonj, Antonellus degli Antonj, Antonello di Giovanni degli Antoni, Antonello degli Antoni, Antonius degli Antoni, Antonellus degli Antoni, Antonello di Giovanni degli Antonello di Giovanni de Antonio, Antonello da Messina. 

The painting is an oil painting on wood and measures 58.0 x 40.0 cm. It was published in 1967 by Sciascia in plates 15 and 16 of his publication "Antonello da Messina". A photograph of the painting is in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.
The administrator of the Washington National Gallery of Art is Washington. The former owner was Robert H. Benson.

The Deposition from the Cross with Saint Peter Martyr is an oil painting on canvas. It was made by Giuseppe Salviati and Giuseppe Maler Porta and is located in the sacristy of the Church of San Pietro Martire in Murano di Venezia. The painting is 73 cm wide, 71 cm high, and 2.11 cm thick. It is housed in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.

A digital photograph of Roberto Sigismondi's work from 1381.197.tif, catalogued as bhex-2022-35-199. The photograph, taken in colour on July 5, 2023, shows the complete work with its frame. It was commissioned by Roberto Sigismondi for order 35/2022. The rights to the work are divided.

The manager of the Palazzo Ducale in Gubbio published a painting of Christ and Nicodemus. The painting dates from between 1846 and 1855 and is an oil painting on canvas. The painting has some imperfections. The Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome has the painting in its collection.
The manager of the Gubbio Palazzo Ducale is the Gubbio Palazzo Ducale.

The tapestry on display depicts a battle scene and was painted in Naples around 1601/1700. It is in the possession of the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica in the Palazzo Barberini in Rome and was acquired in 1895 through the Monte di Pietà. The painting is on canvas and measures 51 x 78 cm. The unsigned work can be found on page 389 of the catalogue "Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica. Palazzo Barberini, i dipinti. Catalogo sistematico" by Onori and Vodret (eds.) from 2008.

The interior facade of the Chiesa dell'Annunziata church in Sant'Agata de' Goti was built around 1404/1414. The fresco of the Last Judgment dates from this period and was restored in 1973/1977. It is tempera on plaster and depicts the scenes of the Last Judgment in three registers.

In the upper register, Christ, the Apostles, Mary, and John the Baptist are depicted. The middle register shows the Resurrection of the Dead on the left and Purgatory on the right. The lower register shows Heaven on the left and Hell on the right.

The upper register shows Christ, the Apostles, Mary, and John the Baptist. In the middle register, on the left, is the Resurrection of the Dead, and on the right, Purgatory. The lower registers show, on the left, heavenly Jerusalem and, on the right, Hell.

The interior facade of the Chiesa dell'Annunziata in Sant'Agata de' Goti was built and restored between 1404/1414 and 1973/1977. A significant fresco depicting the theme of "Last Judgment" adorns the facade. It is a tempera painting on plaster and consists of three registers. 

The upper register shows Christ, the Apostles, Mary, and John the Baptist. The middle register is divided: on the left, the resurrection of the dead, and on the right, purgatory. The lower register depicts on the left, heavenly Jerusalem, and on the right, hell.

The interior facade of the Chiesa dell'Annunziata church in Sant'Agata de' Goti was built and restored between 1404/1414 and 1973/1977. The Last Judgment, a tempera fresco on plaster, covers the entire upper floor. The top register depicts Christ, the Apostles, Mary, and John the Baptist.

The interior facade of the Chiesa dell'Annunziata church in Sant'Agata de' Goti was built and restored between 1404/1414 and 1973/1977. A remarkable fresco of the Last Judgment in tempera on plaster adorns the church.  The upper register depicts Christ, the Apostles, Mary, and John the Baptist. 

The middle register shows the Resurrection of the Dead on the left and Purgatory on the right. The lower register shows heavenly Jerusalem on the left and Hell on the right. The fresco is part of the Bibliotheca Hertziana collection in Rome and was published by C. Frugoni in the 2004 book "Working in Hell".

The interior facade of the Chiesa dell'Annunziata church in Sant'Agata de' Goti was built and restored between 1404/1414 and 1973/1977. The Last Judgment, a tempera painting on plaster, spans the entire facade. The upper register depicts Christ, the Apostles, Mary, and John the Baptist. The middle register on the left shows the Resurrection of the Dead and on the right, Purgatory. The lower register shows Heaven on the left and Hell on the right. 


Descriptions are taken from the work "Lavorare al'inferno" by C. Frugoni (ed.), Bari 2004 and the Bibliotheca Hertziana Rome.

The panel painting "Mourning for the Dead Christ" is located in the Chiesa dell'Annunziata in Sant'Agata de' Goti. The painting, dated 1501/1550, is on canvas and depicts a Campanian scene. It is in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome. The dimensions of the painting are 73 D x 72 12 1 gfr.
A 1964 photograph by Max Hutzel depicts Maria Magdalena in a locked state. The black-and-white photograph originates from "Camp Xart".

The painting exhibition at the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome features an oil painting on canvas depicting the mourning for the dead Christ. The painting originates from Sant'Agata de' Goti and was created around 1501/1550. It is located in the Chiesa dell'Annunziata church and is possibly by Campanisti. The painting measures 73 cm in width and 72 cm in height, with a depth of 12 cm.

The panel painting "The Sorrows of Mary" is located in the Certosa di Trisulti monastery near Trisulti. The painting was created between 1601 and 1700 in the Neapolitan style. It is an oil painting on canvas and measures 11 feet 24 inches 1 gauge. The work is part of the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.

Vodret in the catalogue "Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica. Palazzo Barberini, i dipinti. Catalogo sistematico" from 2008. The Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome holds another copy of the painting.

The oil painting "Saint Maurus of Subiaco" was installed in Petralia Sottana in the Chiesa Madre Santa Maria Assunta church. The painting depicts Saint Maurus of Subiaco and is painted on canvas. The dimensions are 217 x 146 cm. The Allegory of Fortitude with Fides and Caritas is a painting by Giovanni Battista Gaulli, also known as il Bacciccia. It was created around 1668 in Rome and is now located in the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica in the Palazzo Barberini. The work was acquired by the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica in 1916. The oil painting on canvas measures 60 x 50 cm.

In Naples, the painting "Saint Anthony of Padua and Other Saints" is located in the church of Santi Giuseppe e Cristoforo. It was created around 1701/1720 by Nicola Malinconico. The work is an oil painting on canvas.

The painting is 11 H high and is located in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.

A photograph of Hanfstaengl from the period 1940 to 1944 is shown in this listing. It is a rare charcoal print designated "raro-art". The photograph is fully mounted and in good condition. There are two small creases on the back and the stamp is present.

The painting "Madonna with Saints Peter Martyr and Catherine of Alexandria" was painted by the artist Bartolomeo di Maestro Gentile. It was created in the Palazzo Ducale in Urbino. The work was previously attributed to the painter Giovanni Santi.

The "Madonna with Saints Peter Martyr and Catherine of Alexandria" is now in the possession of the curator of the Budapest Museum of Fine Arts.

The curator of the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica in Palazzo Barberini acquired the painting in 1960. It was painted by Giovanni Baglione around 1628 and is a variant of "The Washing of the Apostles". The oil painting on canvas measures 205 x 130 cm and bears the signature "EQV.s IOANNES. BAGLIOINVS. RO. PI. 1628" in the lower left corner. Additionally, the numbering "F. 34" and "L." are also located in the lower left corner. 

The Washing of the Apostles is a well-known motif in art history and has been interpreted by many artists. Giovanni Baglione, an Italian painter of the 17th century, created his own version of this theme. The painting is now in the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica in Rome.
The object custodian is the Rome National Gallery of Ancient Art. The object was acquired in the Palazzo Barberini and dates from 1960.

The painting "Bacchus and Ariadne" is by the Roman painter Francesco Romanelli and was created around 1660. It is an oil painting on canvas measuring 127 x 267 cm. The work is in the possession of the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica in the Palazzo Barberini in Rome and was acquired in 1971.

The publication of the painting can be found in the catalog "Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica. Palazzo Barberini, i dipinti. Catalogo sistematico" published by L. Mochi Onori and R. Vodret, published in 2008 in Rome.

The painting "Visitation" was created around 1688 by Nicolo Russo in Naples. It is now located in the Museo Civico in Castel Nuovo, Naples. The chapel Cappella di San Francesco di Paola, located within Castel Nuovo, was the original site of creation for the painting.
The curator of the Naples Civic Museum in Castel Nuovo is called Naples Civic Museum.

The painting "Pietà" (Vesperbild) was created around 1630/1640 by the Spanish painter Jusepe de Ribera. It is an oil painting on canvas, measuring 73 cm in height and 72 cm in width. The work is currently located in the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome. The artist is also known by the names Giuseppe José de Lo Spagnoletto, Lo El Españoleto, Ribera, José Jusepe de Ribera. The painting was acquired by the curator of the Naples Museum in Castel Nuovo.
The curator of the Naples Civic Museum in Castel Nuovo is called Naples Civic Museum.

The administrator from Montepulciano is located in the Civic Museum in Siena and was created around 1400. The tempera painting on wood depicts the Holy Madonna dell'Umiltà, John the Baptist, Biagio, Louis of Toulouse, or Saint Sigismund. The dimensions of the painting are 74 x 38 cm. The work is part of the collection of the Civic Museum in Siena (Inv. No. 71/131) and was created by Cristofano di Bindoccio detto il Malabarba or an unknown artist.

The attribution to Cristofano di Bindoccio detto il Malabarba has been confirmed by the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome and the Kunsthistorisches Institut in Florence.

The Venetian painter Vittore Carpaccio created the painting "Two Venetian Ladies" around 1504. The oil painting on wood is 164 x 94 cm in size and is located in the Museo Correr e Quadreria Correr in Venice. It is part of the collection "61 BB 2 (TORELLI,?)" and bears the inventory number 12 (+55) 46 A 12 61 E (VENEZIA). 

The depiction was documented in the Bibliotheca Hertziana Rome and in Foto Marburg. Pietro Zampetti included an illustration of the work in his catalog "Vittore Carpaccio, catalogo della mostre" on plate 49.

The painting "Mary with Child and John the Baptist" was dated by the curator of the Museo Civico in Montepulciano to the year 1451/1500. The Florentine painting, executed on a panel, depicts Mary with Child and John the Baptist. The technique of tempera painting on wood is recognizable. The painting measures 81 x 68.5 cm and is in the possession of the Museo Civico Pinacoteca Crociani in Siena. 

The work was first mentioned in the publication "Pinacoteca Crociani, Siena 2000" on page 192. The attribution to an anonymous artist comes from the Bibliotheca Hertziana in Rome.

The curator of the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna in Rome published work 8654, a gift from 1989. The former owner is unknown.
